title.zh: 卷二百八十九 列傳第一百七十七 忠義一
title.raw: 卷二百八十九 列傳第一百七十七 忠義一 Volume 289 Biographies 177: Loyal Officials 1

sentences.zh: 從古忠臣義士，為國捐生，節炳一時，名垂百世，歷代以來，備極表章，尚已。

translations.literal: From ancient times loyal ministers and righteous men have given their lives for the state; their integrity shone for a season and their fame endures for a hundred generations. Through successive dynasties they have been honored to the fullest degree—that is already well established.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, loyal ministers and righteous men have laid down their lives for the state; their integrity blazed for a moment in time, their names live on for a hundred generations, and every dynasty has honored them to the utmost—that much is already settled.

sentences.zh: 明太祖創業江左，首褒余闕、福壽，以作忠義之氣。

translations.literal: When the Ming founder established his enterprise in the lower Yangzi, he first honored Yu Que and Fu Shou to arouse the spirit of loyalty and righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ming founder was building his enterprise in the lower Yangzi, he first honored Yu Que and Fu Shou to stir the spirit of loyalty and righteousness.

sentences.zh: 至從龍將士，或功未就而身亡，若豫章、康郎山兩廟及溪籠山功臣廟所祀諸人，爵贈公侯，血食俎豆，侑享太廟，恤錄子孫，所以褒厲精忠，激揚義烈，意至遠也。

translations.literal: As for the generals who followed the dragon banner, some died before their merit was completed, such as those enshrined at the two temples at Yuzhang and Kanglang Mountain and at the Temple of Meritorious Officials on Xilong Mountain—noble ranks of marquis or duke were posthumously conferred, sacrifices of blood and offerings sustained them, they were honored in the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and their descendants were granted relief and registers—all to encourage refined loyalty and exalt righteous fervor, with intent reaching very far indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Among the generals who followed the founding banner, some died before their achievements were complete—such as those enshrined at the Yuzhang and Kanglangshan temples and at the Xilongshan Temple of Meritorious Officials. They were posthumously ennobled as marquises or dukes, received blood sacrifices and offerings, were honored in the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and had their descendants recorded for relief—all to reward refined loyalty and rouse righteous fervor, with a purpose that reached very far indeed.

sentences.zh: 建文之變，群臣不憚膏鼎鑊，赤姻族，以抗成祖之威棱，雖《表忠》一錄出自傳疑，亦足以知人心天性之不泯矣。

translations.literal: At the upheaval of the Jianwen reign, court officials did not shrink from the cauldron and boiling oil or from having their entire clans exterminated, in order to resist the awe-inspiring force of the Chengzu emperor; though the record "Manifesting Loyalty" arose from disputed tradition, it is enough to show that the human heart and innate nature had not been extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianwen upheaval, officials did not shrink from the cauldron and the boiling cauldron or from having their whole clans wiped out in order to defy the Chengzu emperor's overwhelming might. Though the record "Manifesting Loyalty" rests on disputed tradition, it is enough to show that human hearts and innate nature had not been extinguished.

sentences.zh: 仁宣以降，重熙累洽，垂二百余載，中間如交阯之征，土木之變，宸濠之叛，以暨神、熹兩朝，邊陲多故，沈身殉難者，未易更仆數。

translations.literal: From the Ren-Xuan era onward, amid successive eras of radiance and harmony extending over more than two hundred years, in between came campaigns such as that in Jiaozhi, the Tumu crisis, and Prince Ning's rebellion, as well as the two reigns of Shenzong and Xizong—on the frontiers crises multiplied, and those who sank their bodies and died for their country are not easily counted by the dozen.
translations.idiomatic: From the Hongxi and Xuande reigns onward, through more than two centuries of repeated peace and prosperity, there were nevertheless campaigns such as that in Jiaozhi, the Tumu disaster, and the Prince of Ning's rebellion, and under the Shenzong and Xizong reigns the frontiers saw constant trouble. Those who gave their lives in sacrifice are not easily counted in tens.

sentences.zh: 而司勛褒恤之典，悉從優厚。

translations.literal: Yet the Ministry of Rites' regulations for honoring and comforting the dead were uniformly generous.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Ministry of Rites' rites of commendation and condolence were uniformly generous in every case.

sentences.zh: 或所司失奏，後人得自陳請。

translations.literal: When the responsible office failed to memorialize the throne, later persons could plead on their own behalf.
translations.idiomatic: When the responsible office failed to report a case to the throne, later generations could petition on their own behalf.

sentences.zh: 故節烈之績，鹹得顯暴於時。

translations.literal: Thus deeds of integrity and martyrdom all came to be made manifest in their own time.
translations.idiomatic: Thus deeds of integrity and martyrdom could all be made known in their own day.

sentences.zh: 迨莊烈之朝，運丁陽九，時則內外諸臣，或隕首封疆，或致命闕下，蹈死如歸者尤眾。

translations.literal: When it came to the reign of the Chongzhen emperor, the dynasty met the ninth yang calamity; at that time, whether in the provinces or at court, officials either lost their heads on the frontier or gave their lives beneath the palace gates—those who embraced death as if returning home were especially numerous.
translations.idiomatic: By the reign of the Chongzhen emperor, the dynasty had reached the ninth yang calamity. Officials within and without the court—some losing their heads on the frontier, some giving their lives at the palace gates—were especially numerous among those who went to their deaths as if returning home.

sentences.zh: 今就有明一代死義死事之臣，博采旁搜，匯次如左。

translations.literal: Now, taking the officials of the Ming who died for righteousness or for the state throughout the dynasty, I have gathered widely and searched broadly and arranged them below.
translations.idiomatic: Here, concerning officials of the Ming who died for righteousness or in the line of duty throughout the dynasty, I have gathered widely from many sources and arranged them below.

sentences.zh: 同死者，各因事附見。

translations.literal: Those who died together are each noted in connection with the relevant affair.
translations.idiomatic: Those who died together are each mentioned in connection with the relevant event.

sentences.zh: 其事實繁多及國家興亡所系，或連屬他傳，本末始著，與夫直諫死忠，疏草傳誦人口，概具前帙。

translations.literal: Where the facts are numerous or bear on the rise and fall of the state, the account may extend into other biographies before the beginning and end become clear; as for those who remonstrated bluntly and died loyal, whose memorials are on everyone's lips, these are largely contained in earlier volumes.
translations.idiomatic: Where the facts are numerous or bear on the rise and fall of the state, the narrative may run on into other biographies before the full story emerges. As for those who remonstrated bluntly and died loyal, whose memorials everyone recites, these are largely covered in earlier volumes.

sentences.zh: 至若抒忠勝國，抗命興朝，稽諸前史，例得並書。

translations.literal: As for those who expressed loyalty to a fallen state and resisted orders in founding a new dynasty, according to earlier histories they may be written together by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: As for those who showed loyalty to a fallen state and defied orders to serve a rising dynasty, precedent in earlier histories allows them to be recorded together.

sentences.zh: 我太祖、太宗忠厚開基，扶植名教，獎張銓之守義，釋張春而加禮，洪量同天地，大義懸日月，國史所載，煥若丹青。

translations.literal: Our Taizu and Taizong, in founding the dynasty with generosity and magnanimity, upheld the name and teaching; they rewarded Zhang Quan's steadfast loyalty and released Zhang Chun to honor him—their vast tolerance matched heaven and earth, their great righteousness hung like sun and moon; what the dynastic history records shines like paintings in cinnabar and blue.
translations.idiomatic: Our Taizu and Taizong founded the dynasty with generosity and magnanimity, upheld the moral order, rewarded Zhang Quan for holding to righteousness, and released Zhang Chun to honor him. Their vast forbearance matched heaven and earth; their great righteousness hung like sun and moon. What the dynastic history records shines like paintings in red and blue.

sentences.zh: 諸臣之遂誌成仁，斯為無忝，故備列焉。

translations.literal: That these officials fulfilled their will and achieved humanity is without dishonor—therefore they are all listed here.
translations.idiomatic: That these officials fulfilled their purpose and achieved humanity is without shame—therefore they are all listed here in full.

sentences.zh: 花雲，懷遠人。

translations.literal: Hua Yun was a native of Huaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Hua Yun was a native of Huaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 貌偉而黑，驍勇絕倫。

translations.literal: His appearance was imposing and dark, and his valor in battle was unmatched.
translations.idiomatic: He was imposing in stature and dark in complexion, and his valor in battle was unmatched.

sentences.zh: 至正十三年癸巳，杖劍謁太祖於臨濠。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhizheng, the year guisi, he took sword in hand and called on the founder at Linhao.
translations.idiomatic: In 1353, sword in hand, he presented himself to the founder at Linhao.

sentences.zh: 奇其才，俾將兵略地，所至輒克。

translations.literal: The founder marveled at his talent and had him lead troops to seize territory; wherever he went he prevailed.
translations.idiomatic: The founder was struck by his talent and put him in command of troops to seize territory; wherever he went, he prevailed.

sentences.zh: 破懷遠，擒其帥。

translations.literal: He took Huaiyuan and captured its commander.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Huaiyuan and took its commander prisoner.

sentences.zh: 攻全椒，拔之。

translations.literal: He attacked Quanjiao and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Quanjiao and took it.

sentences.zh: 襲繆家寨，群寇散走。

translations.literal: He raided Miaojia Stockade and the bandits scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: He raided Miaojia Stockade, and the bandits scattered and fled.

sentences.zh: 太祖將取滁州，率數騎前行，雲從。

translations.literal: When the founder was about to take Chuzhou, he led a few horsemen forward and Yun followed.
translations.idiomatic: When the founder was about to take Chuzhou, he rode ahead with a few horsemen, and Yun went with him.

sentences.zh: 猝遇賊數千，雲舉鈹翼太祖，拔劍躍馬沖陣而進。

translations.literal: Suddenly they met several thousand bandits; Yun raised his halberd to shield the founder, drew his sword, spurred his horse, and charged into the enemy ranks.
translations.idiomatic: They suddenly encountered several thousand bandits. Yun raised his halberd to shield the founder, drew his sword, spurred his horse, and charged straight into the enemy formation.

sentences.zh: 賊驚曰：「此黑將軍勇甚，不可當其鋒。」

translations.literal: The bandits cried in alarm: This black general is exceedingly brave—we cannot withstand his charge.”
translations.idiomatic: The bandits cried in alarm, "This black general is exceedingly brave—we cannot withstand his charge.”

sentences.zh: 兵至，遂克滁州。

translations.literal: When the troops arrived, Chuzhou was captured.
translations.idiomatic: When reinforcements arrived, they took Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 甲午從取和州，獲卒三百，以功授管勾。

translations.literal: In the year jiawu he followed in the capture of Hezhou, took three hundred enemy soldiers, and for his merit was appointed registrar.
translations.idiomatic: In 1354 he followed in the capture of Hezhou, took three hundred enemy soldiers prisoner, and was appointed registrar for his merit.

sentences.zh: 乙未，太祖渡江，雲先濟。

translations.literal: In the year yiwei the founder crossed the Yangzi, and Yun crossed first.
translations.idiomatic: In 1355, when the founder crossed the Yangzi, Yun crossed ahead of him.

sentences.zh: 既克太平，以忠勇宿衛左右。

translations.literal: After Taiping was taken, because of his loyalty and courage he was assigned to guard the founder day and night.
translations.idiomatic: After Taiping was taken, his loyalty and courage won him a place in the founder's personal guard.

sentences.zh: 從下集慶，獲卒三千，擢總管。

translations.literal: He followed in the reduction of Jiqing, captured three thousand soldiers, and was promoted to commander.
translations.idiomatic: He followed in the capture of Jiqing, took three thousand soldiers prisoner, and was promoted to commander.

sentences.zh: 徇鎮江、丹陽、丹徒、金壇，皆克之。

translations.literal: He campaigned through Zhenjiang, Danyang, Dantu, and Jintan, and captured them all.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned through Zhenjiang, Danyang, Dantu, and Jintan and captured them all.

sentences.zh: 過馬馱沙，劇盜數百遮道索戰。

translations.literal: Passing Matuosha, several hundred fierce bandits blocked the road and demanded battle.
translations.idiomatic: At Matuosha, several hundred fierce bandits blocked the road and challenged him to fight.

sentences.zh: 雲且行且鬥三日夜，皆擒殺之，授前部先鋒。

translations.literal: Yun fought as he marched for three days and nights, captured and killed them all, and was appointed vanguard of the forward division.
translations.idiomatic: Yun fought as he marched for three days and nights, captured and killed them all, and was made vanguard of the forward division.

sentences.zh: 從拔常州，守牛塘營。

translations.literal: He followed in the capture of Changzhou and garrisoned Niutang Camp.
translations.idiomatic: He followed in the capture of Changzhou and was posted to garrison Niutang Camp.

sentences.zh: 太祖立行樞密院於太平，擢雲院判。

translations.literal: When the founder established the Mobile Bureau of Military Affairs at Taiping, Yun was promoted to vice-director of the bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When the founder established the Mobile Bureau of Military Affairs at Taiping, Yun was promoted to vice-director of the bureau.

sentences.zh: 丁酉克常熟，獲卒萬余。

translations.literal: In the year dingyou he captured Changshu and took more than ten thousand soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In 1357 he captured Changshu and took more than ten thousand soldiers prisoner.

sentences.zh: 命趨寧國，兵陷山澤中八日，群盜相結梗道。

translations.literal: He was ordered to hurry to Ningguo; the army was trapped in mountains and marshes for eight days while bandits banded together to block the road.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to hurry to Ningguo, his troops were trapped in mountains and marshes for eight days while bandits banded together to block the roads.

sentences.zh: 雲操矛鼓噪出入，斬首千百計，身不中一矢。

translations.literal: Yun wielded his spear, shouting as he went in and out, and cut off heads by the hundreds and thousands, yet not a single arrow struck his body.
translations.idiomatic: Yun wielded his spear and charged in and out with battle cries, cutting off heads by the hundreds and thousands, yet not a single arrow struck him.

sentences.zh: 還駐太平。

translations.literal: He returned to garrison Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: He returned to garrison Taiping.

sentences.zh: 庚子閏五月，陳友諒以舟師來寇。

translations.literal: In the intercalary fifth month of the year gengzi, Chen Youliang came to attack with a fleet.
translations.idiomatic: In the intercalary fifth month of 1360, Chen Youliang attacked with a fleet.

sentences.zh: 雲與元帥朱文遜、知府許瑗、院判王鼎結陣迎戰，文遜戰死。

translations.literal: Yun, together with Marshal Zhu Wensun, Prefect Xu Yuan, and Vice-Director Wang Ding, formed battle lines to meet the attack; Wensun died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: Yun, together with Marshal Zhu Wensun, Prefect Xu Yuan, and Vice-Director Wang Ding, formed battle lines to meet the attack. Wensun died in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 賊攻三日不得入，以巨舟乘漲，緣舟尾攀堞而上。

translations.literal: The enemy attacked for three days without breaking in; then with great ships riding the flood tide they climbed the battlements from the sterns of the vessels.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy attacked for three days without breaking in, then used great ships riding the flood tide to climb the battlements from their sterns.

sentences.zh: 城陷，賊縛雲。

translations.literal: The city fell and the enemy bound Yun.
translations.idiomatic: The city fell, and the enemy bound Yun.

sentences.zh: 雲奮身大呼，縛盡裂，起奪守者刀，殺五六人，罵曰：「賊非吾主敵，盍趣降！」

translations.literal: Yun strained his body and shouted; his bonds all split apart. He rose, seized a guard's sword, and killed five or six men, cursing: You bandits are no match for my lord—why not hurry and surrender!”
translations.idiomatic: Yun strained and shouted; his bonds split apart. He rose, seized a guard's sword, and killed five or six men, crying, "You bandits are no match for my lord—why not hurry and surrender!”

sentences.zh: 賊怒，碎其首，縛諸檣叢射之，罵賊不少變，至死聲猶壯，年三十有九。

translations.literal: The enemy in rage smashed his skull, bound him to the mast cluster, and shot at him; he cursed the bandits without the least change, and until death his voice remained strong. He was thirty-nine years old.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the enemy smashed his skull, bound him to the mast cluster, and shot at him. He cursed the bandits without wavering, and until death his voice remained strong. He was thirty-nine years old.

sentences.zh: 瑗、鼎亦抗罵死。

translations.literal: Yuan and Ding also resisted with curses and died.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan and Ding also defied the enemy with curses and died.

sentences.zh: 太祖即吳王位，追封雲東丘郡侯，瑗高陽郡侯，鼎太原郡侯，立忠臣祠，並祀之。

translations.literal: When the founder assumed the title of King of Wu, he posthumously enfeoffed Yun as Marquis of Dongqiu Commandery, Yuan as Marquis of Gaoyang Commandery, and Ding as Marquis of Taiyuan Commandery, and established the Temple of Loyal Ministers to sacrifice to them together.
translations.idiomatic: When the founder assumed the title of King of Wu, he posthumously enfeoffed Yun as Marquis of Dongqiu, Yuan as Marquis of Gaoyang, and Ding as Marquis of Taiyuan, and established the Temple of Loyal Ministers to honor them together.

sentences.zh: 方戰急，雲妻郜祭家廟，挈三歲兒，泣語家人曰：「城破，吾夫必死，吾義不獨存，然不可使花氏無後，若等善撫之。」

translations.literal: While the battle was fierce, Yun's wife Gao sacrificed at the family shrine, took her three-year-old son, and weeping said to the household: When the city falls my husband will surely die; by righteousness I cannot live alone, yet the Hua line must not be cut off—you must raise him well.”
translations.idiomatic: While the battle raged, Yun's wife Gao sacrificed at the family shrine, took her three-year-old son, and weeping told the household, "When the city falls, my husband will surely die. By righteousness I cannot live alone, yet the Hua line must not end—you must raise him well.”

sentences.zh: 雲被執，郜赴水死。

translations.literal: When Yun was captured, Gao threw herself into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: When Yun was captured, Gao threw herself into the water and died.

sentences.zh: 侍兒孫瘞畢，抱兒行，被掠至九江。

translations.literal: The maid Sun buried her and then, carrying the child, set out but was seized and taken to Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: The maid Sun buried her, then set out carrying the child but was seized and taken to Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 孫夜投漁家，脫簪珥屬養之。

translations.literal: At night Sun went to a fisherman's household, removed her hairpins and earrings, and entrusted them to raise the child.
translations.idiomatic: At night Sun went to a fisherman's home, removed her hairpins and earrings, and left the child in their care.

sentences.zh: 及漢兵敗，孫復竊兒走渡江，遇僨軍奪舟棄江中，浮斷木入葦洲，采蓮實哺兒，七日不死。

translations.literal: When the Han army was defeated, Sun again stole away with the child to cross the river; they met disorderly troops who seized the boat and cast them into the river. They floated on a broken timber into a reed marsh, gathered lotus seeds to feed the child, and for seven days did not die.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Youliang's army was defeated, Sun stole away with the child to cross the river again. Disorderly troops seized their boat and cast them into the river. They floated on a broken timber into a reed marsh, gathered lotus seeds to feed the child, and for seven days they did not die.

sentences.zh: 夜半，有老父雷老挈之行，逾年達太祖所。

translations.literal: At midnight an old man, Old Man Lei, took them along; after more than a year they reached the founder's camp.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight an old man called Old Man Lei took them along, and after more than a year they reached the founder's camp.

sentences.zh: 孫抱兒拜泣，太祖亦泣，置兒膝上，曰：「將種也。」

translations.literal: Sun embraced the child and bowed weeping; the founder wept as well, set the child on his knee, and said: The seed of a general.”
translations.idiomatic: Sun embraced the child and bowed, weeping. The founder wept as well, set the child on his knee, and said, "The seed of a general.”

sentences.zh: 賜雷老衣，忽不見。

translations.literal: He gave Old Man Lei a robe, and suddenly he was gone.
translations.idiomatic: He gave Old Man Lei a robe, and suddenly the old man was gone.

sentences.zh: 賜兒名煒，累官水軍衛指揮僉事。

translations.literal: He bestowed on the child the name Wei, and through successive promotions he rose to assistant commander of the Naval Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The founder named the child Wei, who rose through successive promotions to assistant commander of the Naval Guard.

sentences.zh: 其五世孫為遼復州衛指揮，請於世宗，贈郜貞烈夫人，孫安人，立祠致祭。

translations.literal: His fifth-generation descendant served as commander of the Liaofu Guard in Liaoning; he petitioned the Shizong emperor, and Lady Gao was posthumously granted the title Chaste and Fierce Lady, Lady Sun the title Madame, and a shrine was erected for sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: His fifth-generation descendant served as commander of the Liaofu Guard in Liaoning. He petitioned the Shizong emperor, who posthumously granted Lady Gao the title Chaste and Fierce Lady and Lady Sun the title Madame, and had a shrine erected for their veneration.

sentences.zh: 文遜者，太祖養子也。

translations.literal: Wensun was an adopted son of the founder.
translations.idiomatic: Wensun was an adopted son of the founder.

sentences.zh: 嘗與元帥秦友諒攻克無為州。

translations.literal: He once joined Marshal Qin Youliang in capturing Wuwei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He once joined Marshal Qin Youliang in capturing Wuwei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 瑗，字栗夫，樂平人。

translations.literal: Yuan, styled Lifu, was a native of Leping.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan, styled Lifu, was a native of Leping.

sentences.zh: 元末，兩舉鄉第一。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuan, he twice placed first in the provincial examinations.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuan dynasty, he twice placed first in the provincial examinations.

sentences.zh: 太祖駐婺州，瑗謁曰：「足下欲定天下，非延攬英雄，難以成功。」

translations.literal: When the founder was stationed at Wuzhou, Yuan called on him and said: You, sir, wish to pacify the world; unless you extend invitation to heroes, it will be hard to succeed.”
translations.idiomatic: When the founder was stationed at Wuzhou, Yuan called on him and said, "You, sir, wish to pacify the world; unless you gather heroes to your cause, you will find it hard to succeed.”

sentences.zh: 太祖喜，置幕中，參軍事。

translations.literal: The founder was pleased, placed him in his staff, and had him participate in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The founder was pleased, placed him on his staff, and had him participate in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 已，命守太平。

translations.literal: Later he was ordered to guard Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was ordered to guard Taiping.

sentences.zh: 鼎，儀征人。

translations.literal: Ding was a native of Yizheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ding was a native of Yizheng.

sentences.zh: 初為趙忠養子。

translations.literal: At first he was the adopted son of Zhao Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was the adopted son of Zhao Zhong.

sentences.zh: 忠為總管，克太平，授行樞密院判，鎮池州。

translations.literal: Zhong served as zongguan, captured Taiping, was appointed vice-director of the Mobile Bureau of Military Affairs, and garrisoned Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong served as zongguan, captured Taiping, was appointed vice-director of the Mobile Bureau of Military Affairs, and garrisoned Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 趙普勝來寇，忠陣歿。

translations.literal: When Zhao Pusheng came to attack, Zhong died in battle formation.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Pusheng came to attack, Zhong died in battle.

sentences.zh: 鼎嗣職，復故姓，駐太平。

translations.literal: Ding succeeded to the post, restored his original surname, and was stationed at Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: Ding succeeded to the post, restored his original surname, and was posted at Taiping.

sentences.zh: 至是，三人皆死之。

translations.literal: At this time all three died for the cause.
translations.idiomatic: At this time all three died for the cause.

sentences.zh: 時有劉齊者，以江西行省參政守吉安。

translations.literal: At the time there was one Liu Qi, who as Jiangxi Branch Secretariat associate administrator guarded Ji'an.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Liu Qi, associate administrator of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat, was guarding Ji'an.

sentences.zh: 守將李明道開門納友諒兵，殺參政曾萬中、陳海，執齊及知府宋叔華，脅之降，皆不屈。

translations.literal: The defending general Li Mingdao opened the gates to admit Youliang's troops, killed Associate Administrators Zeng Wanzhong and Chen Hai, seized Qi and Prefect Song Shuhua, and coerced them to surrender; all refused to submit.
translations.idiomatic: The defending general Li Mingdao opened the gates to admit Youliang's troops, killed associate administrators Zeng Wanzhong and Chen Hai, seized Qi and Prefect Song Shuhua, and tried to force them to surrender; all refused.

sentences.zh: 又破臨安，執同知趙天麟，亦不屈，並送友諒所。

translations.literal: They also captured Lin'an and seized Vice Prefect Zhao Tianlin, who likewise refused to submit, and all were sent to Youliang's camp.
translations.idiomatic: They also captured Lin'an and seized Vice Prefect Zhao Tianlin, who likewise refused to submit; all were sent to Youliang's camp.

sentences.zh: 友諒方攻洪都，殺三人徇城下。

translations.literal: Youliang was then attacking Hongdu and had the three men killed and displayed beneath the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Youliang was then attacking Hongdu; he had the three men executed and their bodies displayed beneath the walls.

sentences.zh: 及陷無為州，執知州董曾，曾抗罵不屈，沈之江。

translations.literal: When Wuwei Prefecture fell, he seized Prefect Dong Zeng; Zeng resisted with curses and would not submit, and was drowned in the river.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuwei Prefecture fell, he seized Prefect Dong Zeng. Zeng cursed him and refused to submit, and was drowned in the river.

sentences.zh: 王愷，字用和，當塗人。

translations.literal: Wang Kai, styled Yonghe, was a native of Dangtu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Kai, styled Yonghe, was a native of Dangtu.

sentences.zh: 通經史，為元府吏。

translations.literal: He mastered the classics and histories and served as a Yuan prefectural clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Well versed in the classics and histories, he served as a Yuan prefectural clerk.

sentences.zh: 太祖拔太平，召為掾。

translations.literal: When the founder took Taiping, he summoned Kai and appointed him a staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: When the founder took Taiping, he summoned Kai and appointed him a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 從下京口，撫定新附民。

translations.literal: He followed in the capture of Jingkou and pacified the newly submitted populace.
translations.idiomatic: He followed in the capture of Jingkou and pacified the newly submitted populace.

sentences.zh: 及建中書省，用為都事。

translations.literal: When the Secretariat was established, Kai was appointed chief administrator.
translations.idiomatic: When the Secretariat was established, Kai was appointed chief administrator.

sentences.zh: 杭州苗軍數萬降，待命嚴州境。

translations.literal: Several tens of thousands of Miao troops from Hangzhou surrendered and awaited orders on the border of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Several tens of thousands of Miao troops from Hangzhou surrendered and awaited orders on the Yanzhou border.

sentences.zh: 愷馳諭之，偕其帥至。

translations.literal: Kai hurried to instruct them and came together with their commander.
translations.idiomatic: Kai hurried to instruct them and brought their commander with him.

sentences.zh: 太祖克衢州，命總制軍民事。

translations.literal: When the founder captured Quzhou, he ordered Kai to take overall charge of military and civil affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the founder captured Quzhou, he put Kai in overall charge of military and civil affairs.

sentences.zh: 愷增城浚濠，置遊擊軍，籍丁壯，得萬余人。

translations.literal: Kai raised the walls, dredged the moat, established mobile strike forces, registered able-bodied men, and mustered more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Kai raised the walls, dredged the moat, established mobile strike forces, registered able-bodied men, and mustered more than ten thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 常遇春屯兵金華，部將擾民，愷械而撻諸市。

translations.literal: Chang Yuchun stationed troops at Jinhua; his subordinate officers harassed the people, and Kai put them in cangues and flogged them in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Yuchun had troops stationed at Jinhua; when his subordinate officers harassed the people, Kai put them in cangues and flogged them in the market.

sentences.zh: 遇春讓愷，愷曰：「民者國之本，撻一部將而民安，將軍所樂聞也。」

translations.literal: Yuchun reproached Kai; Kai said: The people are the foundation of the state; to flog one subordinate officer and bring the people peace is something the general would be glad to hear.”
translations.idiomatic: Kai said, “The people are the foundation of the state. To flog one subordinate officer and bring the people peace is something a general would be glad to hear.”

sentences.zh: 乃謝愷。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yuchun apologized to Kai.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Yuchun apologized to Kai.

sentences.zh: 時饑疫相仍，愷出倉粟，修惠濟局，全活無算。

translations.literal: Famine and pestilence followed one upon another; Kai released grain from the granary, restored the Charitable Relief Bureau, and saved innumerable lives.
translations.idiomatic: As famine and pestilence followed one upon another, Kai released grain from the granary, restored the Charitable Relief Bureau, and saved innumerable lives.

sentences.zh: 學校毀，與孔子家廟之在衢者，並新之。

translations.literal: The schools were ruined; together with the Confucian family temple at Quzhou, Kai rebuilt them.
translations.idiomatic: The schools lay in ruins; Kai rebuilt them together with the Confucian family temple at Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 設博士弟子員，士翕然悅服。

translations.literal: He established posts for erudites and student members; the scholars all rejoiced and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: He established posts for erudites and student members, and the scholars all rejoiced and submitted.

sentences.zh: 開化馬宣、江山楊明並為亂，先後討擒之。

translations.literal: Ma Xuan of Kaihua and Yang Ming of Jiangshan both raised rebellion; Kai successively suppressed and captured them.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Xuan of Kaihua and Yang Ming of Jiangshan both raised rebellion; Kai successively suppressed them and captured them.

sentences.zh: 遷左司郎中，佐胡大海治省事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to left secretariat director and assisted Hu Dahai in managing provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to left secretariat director and assisted Hu Dahai in managing provincial affairs.

sentences.zh: 苗軍作亂，害大海。

translations.literal: The Miao troops rebelled and killed Dahai.
translations.idiomatic: The Miao troops rebelled and killed Dahai.

sentences.zh: 其帥多德愷，欲擁之而西。

translations.literal: Their commanders mostly favored Kai and wished to install him and march west.
translations.idiomatic: Their commanders mostly favored Kai and wished to install him as leader and march west.

sentences.zh: 愷正色曰：「吾守士，議當死，寧從賊邪！」

translations.literal: Kai said with stern countenance: I am an official charged with defense; by principle I ought to die—would I rather follow bandits!”
translations.idiomatic: Kai said sternly, “I am an official charged with defense. By principle I ought to die—would I follow bandits!”

sentences.zh: 遂並其子行殺之。

translations.literal: Thereupon they killed him together with his son on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon they killed him together with his son on the spot.

sentences.zh: 年四十六。

translations.literal: He was forty-six years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was forty-six years old.

sentences.zh: 愷善謀斷，嘗白事，未聽，卻立戶外，抵暮不去。

translations.literal: Kai was skilled in planning and decision; once when he reported business and was not heard, he withdrew and stood outside the door, and at dusk still did not leave.
translations.idiomatic: Kai was skilled in planning and decision. Once when he reported on business and was not heard, he withdrew and stood outside the door until dusk without leaving.

sentences.zh: 太祖出，怪問之，愷諫如初，卒從其議。

translations.literal: When the founder came out, he asked in surprise; Kai remonstrated as before, and in the end the founder followed his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: When the founder came out, he asked in surprise. Kai remonstrated as before, and in the end the founder followed his proposal.

sentences.zh: 後贈奉直大夫、飛騎尉，追封當塗縣男。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously granted Grand Master of Direct Counsel and Flying Cavalry Commandant, and enfeoffed as Baron of Dangtu County.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was posthumously granted Grand Master of Direct Counsel and Flying Cavalry Commandant, and enfeoffed as Baron of Dangtu County.

sentences.zh: 孫炎，字伯融，句容人。

translations.literal: Sun Yan, styled Borong, was a native of Jurong.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Yan, styled Borong, was a native of Jurong.

sentences.zh: 面鐵色，跛一足。

translations.literal: His face was iron-colored and he limped on one foot.
translations.idiomatic: His face was iron-dark in color and he limped on one foot.

sentences.zh: 談辨風生，雅負經濟。

translations.literal: In conversation and debate he was spirited; he was known for statecraft.
translations.idiomatic: In conversation and debate he was spirited, and he was known for statecraft.

sentences.zh: 與丁復、夏煜遊，有詩名。

translations.literal: He associated with Ding Fu and Xia Yu and had a reputation in poetry.
translations.idiomatic: He associated with Ding Fu and Xia Yu and had a reputation as a poet.

sentences.zh: 太祖下集慶，召見，請招賢豪成大業。

translations.literal: When the founder descended on Jiqing, he summoned Yan and asked him to recruit worthy heroes to complete the great enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: When the founder took Jiqing, he summoned Yan and asked him to recruit worthy heroes to complete the great enterprise.

sentences.zh: 時方建行中書省，用為首掾。

translations.literal: The Branch Secretariat was then being established, and Yan was appointed chief staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: The Branch Secretariat was then being established, and Yan was appointed chief staff officer.

sentences.zh: 從征浙東，授池州同知，進華陽知府，擢行省都事。

translations.literal: He followed the eastern Zhejiang campaign, was appointed vice prefect of Chizhou, advanced to prefect of Huayang, and was promoted to branch secretariat chief administrator.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the eastern Zhejiang campaign, was appointed vice prefect of Chizhou, advanced to prefect of Huayang, and was promoted to branch secretariat chief administrator.

sentences.zh: 克處州，授總制。

translations.literal: When Chuzhou was captured, he was appointed overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: When Chuzhou was captured, he was appointed overall commander.

sentences.zh: 太祖命招劉基、章溢、葉琛等，基不出。

translations.literal: The founder ordered Yan to recruit Liu Ji, Zhang Yi, Ye Chen, and others; Ji did not come out.
translations.idiomatic: The founder ordered Yan to recruit Liu Ji, Zhang Yi, Ye Chen, and others, but Ji would not come out.

sentences.zh: 炎使再往，基遺以寶劍。

translations.literal: Yan was sent again; Ji sent him a treasured sword.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was sent again, and Ji sent him a treasured sword.

sentences.zh: 炎作詩，以為劍當獻天子，斬不順命者，人臣不敢私，封還之。

translations.literal: Yan composed a poem holding that the sword ought to be presented to the Son of Heaven to cut down those who disobey orders, and that a subject must not keep it privately; he sealed it and returned it.
translations.idiomatic: Yan composed a poem arguing that the sword ought to be presented to the Son of Heaven to cut down those who disobey orders, and that a subject must not keep it privately; he sealed it and returned it.

sentences.zh: 遺基書數千言，基始就見，送之建康。

translations.literal: He sent Ji a letter of several thousand words; Ji then came to see him, and Yan escorted him to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Ji a letter of several thousand words; Ji then came to see him, and Yan escorted him to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 時城外皆賊，城守無一兵。

translations.literal: At the time outside the walls bandits were everywhere, and for city defense there was not a single soldier.
translations.idiomatic: At the time bandits were everywhere outside the walls, and the city had not a single soldier for its defense.

sentences.zh: 苗軍作亂，殺院判耿再成，執炎及知府王道同、元帥朱文剛，幽空室，脅降，不屈。

translations.literal: The Miao troops rebelled, killed Vice-Director Geng Zaicheng, seized Yan together with Prefect Wang Daotong and Marshal Zhu Wengang, confined them in an empty room, and coerced them to surrender; they would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: The Miao troops rebelled, killed Vice-Director Geng Zaicheng, seized Yan together with Prefect Wang Daotong and Marshal Zhu Wengang, confined them in an empty room, and tried to force them to surrender; they refused.

sentences.zh: 賊帥賀仁德燖雁鬥酒啖炎，炎且飲且罵。

translations.literal: The bandit commander He Rend broiled goose and offered a goblet of wine to feed Yan; Yan drank even as he cursed.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit commander He Rend broiled goose and offered a goblet of wine for Yan to eat and drink; Yan drank even as he cursed.

sentences.zh: 賊怒，拔刀叱解衣，炎曰：「此紫綺裘，主上所賜，吾當服以死。」

translations.literal: The bandits in rage drew swords and shouted for him to remove his clothes; Yan said: This purple brocade fur coat was bestowed by the sovereign; I shall wear it when I die.”
translations.idiomatic: Yan said, “This purple brocade fur coat was bestowed by the sovereign; I shall wear it when I die.”

sentences.zh: 遂與道同、文剛皆見害，時年四十。

translations.literal: Thereupon he, Daotong, and Wengang were all killed; he was forty years old.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he, Daotong, and Wengang were all killed. He was forty years old.

sentences.zh: 追贈丹陽縣男，建像再成祠。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Baron of Danyang County, and his image was placed in Zaicheng's shrine.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Baron of Danyang County, and his image was placed in Zaicheng's shrine.

sentences.zh: 道同，由中書省宣使在處州，贈太原郡侯。

translations.literal: Daotong, who had been a Secretariat dispatch officer at Chuzhou, was posthumously granted Marquis of Taiyuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Daotong, who had been a Secretariat dispatch officer at Chuzhou, was posthumously granted Marquis of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 文剛，太祖養子，小字柴舍。

translations.literal: Wengang was an adopted son of the founder; his childhood name was Chaishe.
translations.idiomatic: Wengang was an adopted son of the founder; his childhood name was Chaishe.

sentences.zh: 變起，欲與再成聚兵殺賊，不及，遂被難。

translations.literal: When the uprising broke out, he wished to join Zaicheng in gathering troops to kill the bandits but could not arrive in time, and so met disaster.
translations.idiomatic: When the uprising broke out, he wished to join Zaicheng in gathering troops to kill the bandits but could not arrive in time, and so met disaster.

sentences.zh: 贈鎮國將軍，附祭功臣廟。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the State and was included in sacrifice at the Temple of Meritorious Officials.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted General Who Pacifies the State and was included in sacrifice at the Temple of Meritorious Officials.

sentences.zh: 牟魯，烏程人，為莒州同知。

translations.literal: Mou Lu, a native of Wucheng, served as vice prefect of Juzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Mou Lu, a native of Wucheng, served as vice prefect of Juzhou.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年秋，青州民孫古樸為亂，襲州城，執魯欲降之。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the third year of Hongwu, Sun Gupu of Qingzhou raised rebellion, stormed the prefectural city, seized Lu, and wished to make him surrender.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the third year of Hongwu, Sun Gupu of Qingzhou raised rebellion, stormed the prefectural city, seized Lu, and tried to make him surrender.

sentences.zh: 魯曰：「國家混一海字，民皆樂業。

translations.literal: Lu said: The state has unified the empire, and the people all live in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Lu said, “The state has unified the empire, and the people all live in peace.

sentences.zh: 若等悔過自新，可轉禍為福。

translations.literal: If you repent and reform yourselves, you may turn calamity into blessing.
translations.idiomatic: If you repent and reform yourselves, you may turn calamity into blessing.

sentences.zh: 不然，官軍旦夕至，無遺種矣。

translations.literal: Otherwise government troops will arrive within days, and not one of you will survive.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise government troops will arrive within days, and not one of you will survive.

sentences.zh: 我守土臣，義唯一死。」

translations.literal: I am an official charged with guarding this territory; by righteousness I have only death.”
translations.idiomatic: I am an official charged with guarding this territory; by righteousness I have only death.”

sentences.zh: 賊不敢害，擁至城南。

translations.literal: The bandits did not dare harm him but escorted him to the south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits did not dare harm him but escorted him to the south of the city.

sentences.zh: 魯大罵，遂殺之。

translations.literal: Lu cursed loudly and was then killed.
translations.idiomatic: Lu cursed loudly and was then killed.

sentences.zh: 賊破，詔恤其家。

translations.literal: When the bandits were defeated, an edict comforted his family.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits were defeated, an edict was issued to comfort his family.

sentences.zh: 又有白謙、裴源、朱顯忠、王均諒、王名善、黃裏、顧師勝、陳敬、吳得、井孚之屬。

translations.literal: There were also Bai Qian, Pei Yuan, Zhu Xianzhong, Wang Junliang, Wang Mingshan, Huang Li, Gu Shisheng, Chen Jing, Wu De, Jing Fu, and others of that sort.
translations.idiomatic: There were also Bai Qian, Pei Yuan, Zhu Xianzhong, Wang Junliang, Wang Mingshan, Huang Li, Gu Shisheng, Chen Jing, Wu De, Jing Fu, and others of that sort.

sentences.zh: 謙，婺源知州。

translations.literal: Qian was prefect of Wuyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was prefect of Wuyuan.

sentences.zh: 信州盜蕭明來寇，謙力不能禦，懷印出北門，赴水死。

translations.literal: When the Xinzhou bandit Xiao Ming came to attack, Qian could not resist; he took his seal and went out the north gate, threw himself into the water, and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the Xinzhou bandit Xiao Ming came to attack, Qian could not resist. He took his seal, went out the north gate, threw himself into the water, and died.

sentences.zh: 源，肇慶府經歷。

translations.literal: Yuan was administrative aide of Zhaoqing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was administrative aide of Zhaoqing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 以公事赴新興，遇山賊陳勇卿，被執，勒令跪。

translations.literal: On official business he went to Xinxing, encountered the mountain bandit Chen Yongqing, was seized, and was forced to kneel.
translations.idiomatic: On official business he went to Xinxing, encountered the mountain bandit Chen Yongqing, was seized, and was forced to kneel.

sentences.zh: 源大罵曰：「我命官，乃跪賊邪！」

translations.literal: Yuan cursed loudly and said: I am a commissioned official—would I kneel to bandits!”
translations.idiomatic: Yuan cursed loudly and said, “I am a commissioned official—would I kneel to bandits!”

sentences.zh: 遂被殺。

translations.literal: He was then killed.
translations.idiomatic: He was then killed.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年贈官二等。

translations.literal: In the third year of Hongwu he was posthumously promoted two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Hongwu he was posthumously promoted two ranks.

sentences.zh: 顯忠，如臯人。

translations.literal: Xianzhong was a native of Rugao.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong was a native of Rugao.

sentences.zh: 為張士誠將，來降。

translations.literal: He was a general of Zhang Shicheng and came over in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: He had been a general of Zhang Shicheng and came over in surrender.

sentences.zh: 以指揮僉事從鄧愈下河州，抵吐番。

translations.literal: As assistant commander he followed Deng Yu in taking Hezhou and reached Tubo.
translations.idiomatic: As assistant commander he followed Deng Yu in taking Hezhou and reaching Tubo.

sentences.zh: 從傅友德克文州，遂留守之。

translations.literal: He followed Fu Youde in capturing Wenzhou and was then left to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Fu Youde in capturing Wenzhou and was then left to garrison it.

sentences.zh: 洪武四年，蜀將丁世珍召番數萬來攻。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Hongwu, the Shu general Ding Shizhen summoned tens of thousands of fan troops to attack.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Hongwu, the Shu general Ding Shizhen summoned tens of thousands of fan troops to attack.

sentences.zh: 食盡無援，或勸走避，顯忠叱不聽。

translations.literal: When provisions were exhausted and there was no relief, some urged flight; Xianzhong shouted rebukes and would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: When provisions ran out and no relief came, some urged flight; Xianzhong shouted rebukes and would not listen.

sentences.zh: 攻益急，裹創力戰，城破，為亂兵所殺。

translations.literal: As the attack grew fiercer, he bound his wounds and fought with all his strength; when the city fell he was killed by the disorderly troops.
translations.idiomatic: As the attack grew fiercer, he bound his wounds and fought with all his strength. When the city fell he was killed by the disorderly troops.

sentences.zh: 均諒時為千戶，被執不屈，磔死。

translations.literal: Junliang was then a chiliarch, was seized and would not submit, and was executed by dismemberment.
translations.idiomatic: Junliang was then a chiliarch; he was seized, refused to submit, and was executed by dismemberment.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈恤有差。

translations.literal: When the affair was reported, posthumous honors and relief were granted according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: When the affair was reported, posthumous honors and relief were granted according to rank.

sentences.zh: 名善，義烏人，高州通判。

translations.literal: Mingshan, a native of Yiwu, was vice prefect of Gaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Mingshan, a native of Yiwu, was vice prefect of Gaozhou.

sentences.zh: 有海寇何均善曾被戮，洪武四年，其黨羅子仁率眾潛入城，執名善，不屈死。

translations.literal: The sea bandit He Junshan had once been executed; in the fourth year of Hongwu his follower Luo Ziren led a force that secretly entered the city, seized Mingshan, and he died without submitting.
translations.idiomatic: The sea bandit He Junshan had once been executed. In the fourth year of Hongwu his follower Luo Ziren led a force that secretly entered the city, seized Mingshan, and killed him when he refused to submit.

sentences.zh: 裏，雲內州同知。

translations.literal: Li was vice prefect of Yunnei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Li was vice prefect of Yunnei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 洪武五年秋，蒙古兵突入城。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the fifth year of Hongwu, Mongol troops suddenly entered the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the fifth year of Hongwu, Mongol troops suddenly entered the city.

sentences.zh: 裏率兵蒼戰，死之。

translations.literal: Li led troops in fierce fighting and died.
translations.idiomatic: Li led troops in fierce fighting and died.

sentences.zh: 師勝，興化人，峨眉知縣。

translations.literal: Shisheng, a native of Xinghua, was magistrate of Emei.
translations.idiomatic: Shisheng, a native of Xinghua, was magistrate of Emei.

sentences.zh: 洪武十三年率民兵討賊彭普貴，戰死。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Hongwu he led militia to suppress the bandit Peng Pugui and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Hongwu he led militia to suppress the bandit Peng Pugui and died in battle.

sentences.zh: 詔褒恤。

translations.literal: An edict commended him and granted relief to his family.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commended him and granted relief to his family.

sentences.zh: 敬，增城人。

translations.literal: Jing, a native of Zengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Jing, a native of Zengcheng.

sentences.zh: 洪武十四年舉賢良，為曲靖府經歷，署劍川州事。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Hongwu he was nominated as a worthy and good man, appointed assistant prefect of Qujing Prefecture, and acted as administrator of Jianchuan Subprefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Hongwu he was nominated as a worthy and good man, appointed assistant prefect of Qujing Prefecture, and acted as administrator of Jianchuan Subprefecture.

sentences.zh: 鄰寇來攻，敬禦之。

translations.literal: When neighboring bandits came to attack, Jing defended against them.
translations.idiomatic: When neighboring bandits came to attack, Jing defended against them.

sentences.zh: 官兵寡，欲退，敬瞋目大呼，力戰死。

translations.literal: The government troops were few and wished to retreat; Jing glared, shouted loudly, fought with all his strength, and died.
translations.idiomatic: The government troops were few and wished to retreat; Jing glared, shouted loudly, fought with all his strength, and died.

sentences.zh: 命恤其家。

translations.literal: An order was issued to grant relief to his family.
translations.idiomatic: An order was issued to grant relief to his family.

sentences.zh: 得，全椒人，龍裏守禦所千戶。

translations.literal: De, a native of Quanjiao, was a chiliarch of the Longli Guard and Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: De, a native of Quanjiao, was a chiliarch of the Longli Guard and Garrison.

sentences.zh: 洪武三十年，古州上婆洞蠻作亂，得與鎮守將井孚守城。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of Hongwu the Shangpodong barbarians of Guzhou rebelled; De and the garrison commander Jing Fu defended the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year of Hongwu the Shangpodong barbarians of Guzhou rebelled; De and the garrison commander Jing Fu defended the city.

sentences.zh: 賊燒門急攻，二人開門奮擊，得中毒弩死，孚戰死。

translations.literal: The bandits burned the gate and pressed the attack fiercely; the two men opened the gate and fought with spirit. De died from a poisoned crossbow bolt, and Fu died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits burned the gate and pressed the attack fiercely; the two men opened the gate and fought with spirit. De died from a poisoned crossbow bolt, and Fu died in battle.

sentences.zh: 贈得指揮僉事，孚正千戶，子孫世襲。

translations.literal: De was posthumously granted the title of Assistant Commander, Fu was promoted to Regular Chiliarch, and their descendants were granted hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: De was posthumously granted the title of Assistant Commander, Fu was promoted to Regular Chiliarch, and their descendants were granted hereditary succession.

sentences.zh: 王綱，字性常，余姚人。

translations.literal: Wang Gang, styled Xingchang, was a native of Yuyao.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gang, styled Xingchang, was a native of Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 有文武才。

translations.literal: He possessed both civil and military talent.
translations.idiomatic: He possessed both civil and military talent.

sentences.zh: 善劉基，常語曰：「老夫樂山林，異時得誌，勿以世緣累我。」

translations.literal: He was on good terms with Liu Ji and often said: This old man delights in mountain and forest; when you achieve your ambition someday, do not burden me with worldly entanglements.”
translations.idiomatic: He was on good terms with Liu Ji and often said, “This old man delights in mountain and forest; when you achieve your ambition someday, do not burden me with worldly entanglements.”

sentences.zh: 洪武四年以基薦征至京師，年七十，齒發神色如少壯。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Hongwu he was summoned on Ji's recommendation to the capital; he was seventy, yet his teeth, hair, and complexion were like those of a young man.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Hongwu he was summoned to the capital on Ji's recommendation. He was seventy, yet his teeth, hair, and complexion were those of a young man.

sentences.zh: 太祖異之，策以治道，擢兵部郎。

translations.literal: The Founder found him remarkable, tested him on the way of governance, and promoted him to Secretary in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder found him remarkable, tested him on the way of governance, and promoted him to Secretary in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 潮民弗靖，除廣東參議，督兵餉，嘆曰：「吾命盡此矣。」

translations.literal: When the Chaozhou people were unsettled, he was appointed Vice Commissioner of Guangdong, charged with overseeing troops and supplies. He sighed and said: My life will end here.”
translations.idiomatic: When the Chaozhou people were unsettled, he was appointed Vice Commissioner of Guangdong, charged with overseeing troops and supplies. He sighed and said, “My life will end here.”

sentences.zh: 以書訣家人，攜子彥達行，單舸往諭，潮民叩首服罪。

translations.literal: He wrote farewell letters to his family, took his son Yanda with him, and went alone in a single boat to remonstrate; the Chaozhou people kowtowed and submitted in guilt.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote farewell letters to his family, took his son Yanda with him, and went alone in a single boat to remonstrate; the Chaozhou people kowtowed and submitted in guilt.

sentences.zh: 還抵增城，遇海寇曹真，截舟羅拜，願得為帥。

translations.literal: On the return, reaching Zengcheng, he encountered the sea bandit Cao Zhen, who intercepted his boat, prostrated himself in a circle, and asked that Gang become their leader.
translations.idiomatic: On the return, reaching Zengcheng, he encountered the sea bandit Cao Zhen, who intercepted his boat, prostrated himself in a circle, and asked that Gang become their leader.

sentences.zh: 綱諭以禍福，不從，則奮罵。

translations.literal: Gang admonished them with talk of fortune and disaster; when they would not listen, he cursed them fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Gang admonished them with talk of fortune and disaster; when they would not listen, he cursed them fiercely.

sentences.zh: 賊舁之去，為壇坐綱，日拜請。

translations.literal: The bandits carried him off, set up an altar with Gang seated upon it, and daily bowed and entreated him.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits carried him off, set up an altar with Gang seated upon it, and daily bowed and entreated him.

sentences.zh: 綱罵不絕聲，遂遇害。

translations.literal: Gang cursed without cease and was thereupon killed.
translations.idiomatic: Gang cursed without cease and was thereupon killed.

sentences.zh: 彥達年十六，罵賊求死，欲並殺之。

translations.literal: Yanda was sixteen; he cursed the bandits and sought death, wishing to be killed along with his father.
translations.idiomatic: Yanda was sixteen; he cursed the bandits and sought death, wishing to be killed along with his father.

sentences.zh: 其酋曰：「父忠子孝，殺之不詳。」

translations.literal: Their chieftain said: The father is loyal and the son filial—to kill them would be inauspicious.”
translations.idiomatic: Their chieftain said, “The father is loyal and the son filial—to kill them would be inauspicious.”

sentences.zh: 與之食，不顧，令綴羊革裹父屍而出。

translations.literal: They offered him food, but he paid no heed; they had sheep hide sewn together to wrap his father's corpse and let him depart.
translations.idiomatic: They offered him food, but he paid no heed; they had sheep hide sewn together to wrap his father's corpse and let him depart.

sentences.zh: 御史郭純以聞，詔立廟死所。

translations.literal: Censor Guo Chun reported the affair, and an edict ordered a temple erected at the place of his death.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Guo Chun reported the affair, and an edict ordered a temple erected at the place of his death.

sentences.zh: 彥達以蔭得官，痛父，終身不仕。

translations.literal: Yanda obtained office through hereditary privilege, but grieving for his father, he never served for the rest of his life.
translations.idiomatic: Yanda obtained office through hereditary privilege, but grieving for his father, he never served for the rest of his life.

sentences.zh: 王祎，字子充，義烏人。

translations.literal: Wang Yi, style name Zichong, a native of Yiwu.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi, style name Zichong, was a native of Yiwu.

sentences.zh: 幼敏慧，及長，身長嶽立，屹有偉度。

translations.literal: As a child he was quick and intelligent; when grown, he stood tall as a mountain peak, with an imposing and lofty bearing.
translations.idiomatic: As a child he was quick and intelligent; when grown, he stood tall as a mountain peak, with an imposing and lofty bearing.

sentences.zh: 師柳貫、黃溍，遂以文章名世。

translations.literal: He studied under Liu Guan and Huang Jin, and thereby made a name in literary writing throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Liu Guan and Huang Jin, and thereby made a name in literary writing throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 睹元政衰敝，為書七八千言上時宰。

translations.literal: Seeing the Yuan regime decline and decay, he wrote a memorial of seven or eight thousand characters and submitted it to the chief ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the Yuan regime decline and decay, he wrote a memorial of seven or eight thousand characters and submitted it to the chief ministers.

sentences.zh: 危素、張起巖並薦，不報。

translations.literal: Wei Su and Zhang Qiyan both recommended him, but no response came.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Su and Zhang Qiyan both recommended him, but no response came.

sentences.zh: 隱青巖山，著書，名日盛。

translations.literal: He withdrew to Mount Qingyan, wrote books, and his fame grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew to Mount Qingyan, wrote books, and his fame grew daily.

sentences.zh: 太祖取婺州，召見，用為中書省掾史。

translations.literal: When the Founder took Wuzhou, he summoned Yi and appointed him a secretary in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder took Wuzhou, he summoned Yi and appointed him a secretary in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 征江西，祎獻頌。

translations.literal: During the campaign against Jiangxi, Yi presented a eulogy.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Jiangxi, Yi presented a eulogy.

sentences.zh: 太祖喜曰：「江南有二儒，卿與宋濂耳。

translations.literal: The Founder said with pleasure: "In Jiangnan there are two Confucian scholars—you and Song Lian.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder said with pleasure, "In Jiangnan there are two Confucian scholars—you and Song Lian.

sentences.zh: 學問之博，卿不如濂。

translations.literal: In breadth of learning, you are not the equal of Lian.
translations.idiomatic: In breadth of learning, you are not the equal of Lian.

sentences.zh: 才思之雄，濂不如卿。」

translations.literal: In force of talent and thought, Lian is not your equal."
translations.idiomatic: In force of talent and thought, Lian is not your equal."

sentences.zh: 太祖創禮賢館，李文忠薦祎及許元、王天錫，召置館中。

translations.literal: The Founder established the Hall of Honored Worthies. Li Wenzhong recommended Yi together with Xu Yuan and Wang Tiansi, and they were summoned and placed in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder established the Hall of Honored Worthies. Li Wenzhong recommended Yi together with Xu Yuan and Wang Tiansi, and they were summoned and placed in the hall.

sentences.zh: 旋授江南儒學提舉司校理，累遷侍禮郎，掌起居註。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed proofreader of the Jiangnan Education Intendant Office, then successively promoted to Gentleman of Ceremonial Attendance in charge of the Veritable Records of Daily Life.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed proofreader of the Jiangnan Education Intendant Office, then successively promoted to Gentleman of Ceremonial Attendance in charge of the Veritable Records of Daily Life.

sentences.zh: 同知南康府事，多惠政，賜金帶寵之。

translations.literal: As vice magistrate of Nankang Prefecture he enacted many benevolent policies, and was favored with the gift of a gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: As vice magistrate of Nankang Prefecture he enacted many benevolent policies, and was favored with the gift of a gold belt.

sentences.zh: 太祖將即位，召還，議禮。

translations.literal: When the Founder was about to ascend the throne, Yi was recalled to debate ceremonial matters.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founder was about to ascend the throne, Yi was recalled to debate ceremonial matters.

sentences.zh: 坐事忤旨，出為漳州府通判。

translations.literal: For an offense that ran counter to imperial will, he was demoted and sent out as assistant prefect of Zhangzhou Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For an offense that ran counter to imperial will, he was demoted and sent out as assistant prefect of Zhangzhou Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年八月，上疏言：「祈天永命之要，在忠厚以存心，寬大以為政，法天道，順人心。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Hongwu, he submitted a memorial stating: The essential means of praying Heaven for enduring mandate lies in keeping a sincere and generous heart, governing with magnanimity, taking Heaven's Way as model, and conforming to the people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the first year of Hongwu, he submitted a memorial stating, “The essential means of praying Heaven for enduring mandate lies in keeping a sincere and generous heart, governing with magnanimity, taking Heaven's Way as model, and conforming to the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 雷霆霜雪，可暫不可常。

translations.literal: Thunder, frost, and snow may be applied briefly but cannot be constant.
translations.idiomatic: Thunder, frost, and snow may be applied briefly but cannot be constant.

sentences.zh: 浙西既平，科斂當減。」

translations.literal: Now that western Zhejiang is pacified, levies and exactions should be reduced.”
translations.idiomatic: Now that western Zhejiang is pacified, levies and exactions should be reduced.”

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉納之，然不能盡從也。

translations.literal: The Founder commended and accepted it, yet could not fully follow it.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder commended and accepted it, yet could not fully follow it.

sentences.zh: 明年修《元史》，命祎與濂為總裁。

translations.literal: The next year, when the History of Yuan was compiled, Yi and Lian were appointed chief compilers.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when the History of Yuan was compiled, Yi and Lian were appointed chief compilers.

sentences.zh: 祎史事擅長，裁煩剔穢，力任筆削。

translations.literal: Yi excelled at historical matters, cut away redundancy and excised corruption, and personally bore the burden of the brush.
translations.idiomatic: Yi excelled at historical matters, cut away redundancy and excised corruption, and personally bore the burden of the brush.

sentences.zh: 書成，擢翰林待制，同知制誥兼國史院編修官。

translations.literal: When the book was completed, he was promoted to Hanlin Attendant Draftsman, Concurrent Director of Edicts and Compilers, and Compiler at the National History Academy.
translations.idiomatic: When the book was completed, he was promoted to Hanlin Attendant Draftsman, Concurrent Director of Edicts and Compilers, and Compiler at the National History Academy.

sentences.zh: 奉詔預教大本堂，經明理達，善開導。

translations.literal: By imperial order he assisted in teaching at the Daben Hall; his command of the classics was clear and his grasp of principle penetrating, and he was skilled at guidance.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order he assisted in teaching at the Daben Hall; his command of the classics was clear and his grasp of principle penetrating, and he was skilled at guidance.

sentences.zh: 召對殿廷，必賜坐，從容宴語。

translations.literal: When summoned to audience in the palace hall, he was always granted a seat and conversed at leisure over banquet talk.
translations.idiomatic: When summoned to audience in the palace hall, he was always granted a seat and conversed at leisure over banquet talk.

sentences.zh: 未久，奉使吐蕃，未至，召還。

translations.literal: Before long he was sent on mission to Tibet; before arriving he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was sent on mission to Tibet; before arriving he was recalled.

sentences.zh: 五年正月議招諭雲南，命祎賫詔往。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, when persuasion of Yunnan was discussed, Yi was ordered to carry the edict there.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year, when persuasion of Yunnan was discussed, Yi was ordered to carry the edict there.

sentences.zh: 至則諭梁王，亟宜奉版圖歸職方，不然天討旦夕至。

translations.literal: Upon arrival he remonstrated with the Prince of Liang that he should promptly submit his territories to the Ministry of Revenue, or else Heaven's punishment would arrive within days.
translations.idiomatic: Upon arrival he remonstrated with the Prince of Liang that he should promptly submit his territories to the Ministry of Revenue, or else Heaven's punishment would arrive within days.

sentences.zh: 王不聽，館別室。

translations.literal: The prince would not listen and lodged him in a separate chamber.
translations.idiomatic: The prince would not listen and lodged him in a separate chamber.

sentences.zh: 他日，又諭曰：「朝廷以雲南百萬生靈，不欲殲於鋒刃。

translations.literal: Another day he remonstrated again, saying: The court, for the sake of Yunnan's million living souls, does not wish to see them slaughtered on sword's edge.
translations.idiomatic: Another day he remonstrated again, saying, “The court, for the sake of Yunnan's million living souls, does not wish to see them slaughtered on sword's edge.

sentences.zh: 若恃險遠，抗明命，龍驤鹢艫，會戰昆明，悔無及矣。」

translations.literal: If you rely on your terrain's peril and distance and resist the bright mandate, dragon ships and oar-warships will meet in battle at Kunming—and regret will come too late.”
translations.idiomatic: If you rely on your terrain's peril and distance and resist the bright mandate, dragon ships and oar-warships will meet in battle at Kunming—and regret will come too late.”

sentences.zh: 梁王駭服，即為改館。

translations.literal: The Prince of Liang was awed into submission and immediately had his lodging changed.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Liang was awed into submission and immediately had his lodging changed.

sentences.zh: 會元遣脫脫征餉，脅王以危言，必欲殺祎。

translations.literal: At that time the Yuan sent Toktoghan to levy supplies; he threatened the prince with dire words and insisted on killing Yi.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Yuan sent Toktoghan to levy supplies; he threatened the prince with dire words and insisted on killing Yi.

sentences.zh: 王不得已出祎見之，脫脫欲屈祎，祎叱曰：「天既訖汝元命，我朝實代之。

translations.literal: The prince, having no choice, produced Yi to meet him. Toktoghan wished to humiliate Yi; Yi shouted: Heaven has already ended your Yuan mandate, and our dynasty has truly replaced it.
translations.idiomatic: The prince, having no choice, produced Yi to meet him. Toktoghan wished to humiliate Yi; Yi shouted, “Heaven has already ended your Yuan mandate, and our dynasty has truly replaced it.

sentences.zh: 汝爝火余燼，敢與日月爭明邪！

translations.literal: You are embers of a torch-fire—how dare you contend in brightness with sun and moon!
translations.idiomatic: You are embers of a torch-fire—how dare you contend in brightness with sun and moon!

sentences.zh: 且我與汝皆使也，豈為汝屈！」

translations.literal: Moreover, you and I are both envoys—why should I submit to you!”
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, you and I are both envoys—why should I submit to you!”

sentences.zh: 或勸脫脫曰：「王公素負重名，不可害。」

translations.literal: Someone advised Toktoghan: Lord Wang has long borne a weighty reputation—you must not harm him.”
translations.idiomatic: Someone advised Toktoghan, “Lord Wang has long borne a weighty reputation—you must not harm him.”

sentences.zh: 脫脫攘臂曰：「今雖孔聖，義不得存。」

translations.literal: Toktoghan rolled up his sleeves and said: Even if it were Confucius himself, by right he could not be spared.”
translations.idiomatic: Toktoghan rolled up his sleeves and said, “Even if it were Confucius himself, by right he could not be spared.”

sentences.zh: 祎顧王曰：「汝殺我，天兵繼至，汝禍不旋踵矣。」

translations.literal: Yi turned to the prince and said: If you kill me, the celestial army will follow close behind, and disaster will overtake you in no time.”
translations.idiomatic: Yi turned to the prince and said, “If you kill me, the celestial army will follow close behind, and disaster will overtake you in no time.”

sentences.zh: 遂遇害，時十二月二十四日也。

translations.literal: He was thereupon killed—it was the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth month.
translations.idiomatic: He was thereupon killed—it was the twenty-fourth day of the twelfth month.

sentences.zh: 梁王遣使致祭，具衣冠斂之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Liang sent envoys to perform sacrifices and dressed him in cap and gown for burial.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Liang sent envoys to perform sacrifices and dressed him in cap and gown for burial.

sentences.zh: 建文中，祎子紳訟祎事，詔贈翰林學士，謚文節。

translations.literal: During the Jianwen reign, Yi's son Shen petitioned regarding Yi's case; an edict posthumously granted him Hanlin Academician and the posthumous title Wenjie (Cultured Integrity).
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianwen reign, Yi's son Shen petitioned regarding Yi's case; an edict posthumously granted him Hanlin Academician and the posthumous title Wenjie (Cultured Integrity).

sentences.zh: 正統中，改謚忠文。

translations.literal: During the Zhengtong reign the posthumous title was changed to Zhongwen (Loyal Literature).
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengtong reign the posthumous title was changed to Zhongwen (Loyal Literature).

sentences.zh: 成化中，命建祠祀之。

translations.literal: During the Chenghua reign he was ordered a temple built for his veneration.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chenghua reign he was ordered a temple built for his veneration.

sentences.zh: 紳，字仲繕。

translations.literal: Shen, styled Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Shen, styled Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 祎死時，年十三，鞠於兄綬，事母兄盡孝友。

translations.literal: When Yi died, Shen was thirteen; he was raised by his elder brother Shou and served his mother and brother with full filial piety and brotherly affection.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi died, Shen was thirteen; he was raised by his elder brother Shou and served his mother and brother with full filial piety and brotherly affection.

sentences.zh: 長博學，受業宋濂。

translations.literal: When grown he was broadly learned and studied under Song Lian.
translations.idiomatic: When grown he was broadly learned and studied under Song Lian.

sentences.zh: 濂器之曰：「吾友不亡矣。」

translations.literal: Song Lian prized him and said: My friend is not dead after all.”
translations.idiomatic: Song Lian prized him and said, “My friend is not dead after all.”

sentences.zh: 蜀獻王聘紳，待以客禮。

translations.literal: The Prince of Shu invited Shen and treated him with guest ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Shu invited Shen and treated him with guest ceremony.

sentences.zh: 紳啟王往雲南求父遺骸，不獲即死所致祭，述《滇南慟哭記》以歸。

translations.literal: Shen asked the prince to let him go to Yunnan to seek his father's remains; failing to find them, he performed rites at the place of death, composed A Record of Grief in Diannan, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Shen asked the prince to let him go to Yunnan to seek his father's remains; failing to find them, he performed rites at the place of death, composed "A Record of Grief in Diannan," and returned.

sentences.zh: 建文帝時，用薦召為國子博士，預修《太祖實錄》，獻《大明鐃歌鼓吹曲》十二章。

translations.literal: During the Jianwen emperor's reign, on recommendation he was summoned as Erudite of the National University, took part in compiling the Veritable Records of the Founding Emperor, and presented twelve chapters of Great Ming Iron-Club Songs and Processional Airs.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianwen emperor's reign, on recommendation he was summoned as Erudite of the National University, took part in compiling the Veritable Records of the Founding Emperor, and presented twelve chapters of "Great Ming Iron-Club Songs and Processional Airs."

sentences.zh: 與方孝孺友善，卒官。

translations.literal: He was on friendly terms with Fang Xiaoru and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was on friendly terms with Fang Xiaoru and died in office.

sentences.zh: 子稌，字叔豐。

translations.literal: His son Tu, styled Shufeng.
translations.idiomatic: His son Tu, styled Shufeng.

sentences.zh: 師方孝孺。

translations.literal: He studied under Fang Xiaoru.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Fang Xiaoru.

sentences.zh: 孝孺被難，與其友鄭珣輩潛收遣骸，禍幾不測，自是絕意仕進。

translations.literal: When Xiaoru met disaster, Tu and his friends Zheng Xun and others secretly gathered the scattered remains; catastrophe nearly overtook them, and from then on he abandoned all thought of official advancement.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaoru met disaster, Tu and his friends Zheng Xun and others secretly gathered the scattered remains; catastrophe nearly overtook them, and from then on he abandoned all thought of official advancement.

sentences.zh: 初，紳痛父亡，食不兼味。

translations.literal: At first Shen, grieving his father's death, ate without variety of flavors.
translations.idiomatic: At first Shen, grieving his father's death, ate without variety of flavors.

sentences.zh: 稌守之不變，居喪，不飲酒，不食肉者三年，門人私謚曰孝莊先生。

translations.literal: Tu maintained this without change; during mourning he drank no wine and ate no meat for three years, and his disciples privately gave him the posthumous title Master Xiaozhuang (Filial and Stately).
translations.idiomatic: Tu maintained this without change; during mourning he drank no wine and ate no meat for three years, and his disciples privately gave him the posthumous title Master Xiaozhuang (Filial and Stately).

sentences.zh: 子汶，字允達。

translations.literal: His son Wen, styled Yunda.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wen, styled Yunda.

sentences.zh: 成化十四年進士。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Chenghua he passed the metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Chenghua he passed the metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 授中書舍人。

translations.literal: He was appointed Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 謝病歸，讀書齊山下。

translations.literal: He resigned citing illness and returned home to study beneath Mount Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned citing illness and returned home to study beneath Mount Qi.

sentences.zh: 弘治初，言者交薦，與檢討陳獻章同召，未抵京卒。

translations.literal: At the start of the Hongzhi reign, censors repeatedly recommended him; he was summoned together with Compiler Chen Xianzhang, but died before reaching the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Hongzhi reign, censors repeatedly recommended him; he was summoned together with Compiler Chen Xianzhang, but died before reaching the capital.

sentences.zh: 祎死雲南之三年，死事者又有吳雲。

translations.literal: Three years after Yi's death in Yunnan, there was also Wu Yun among those who died in the line of duty.
translations.idiomatic: Three years after Yi's death in Yunnan, there was also Wu Yun among those who died in the line of duty.

sentences.zh: 雲，宜興人。

translations.literal: Yun was a native of Yixing.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was a native of Yixing.

sentences.zh: 元翰林待制，仕太祖，為湖廣行省參政。

translations.literal: He had been Hanlin Attendant Draftsman under the Yuan; he served the Founder as Vice Commissioner of the Huguang Provincial Administration Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He had been Hanlin Attendant Draftsman under the Yuan; he served the Founder as Vice Commissioner of the Huguang Provincial Administration Commission.

sentences.zh: 洪武八年九月，太祖議再遣使招諭梁王，召雲至，語之曰：「今天下一家，獨雲南未奉正朔，殺我使臣，卿能為我作陸賈乎？」

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the eighth year of Hongwu, when the Founder deliberated sending envoys again to persuade the Prince of Liang, he summoned Yun and said to him: Under Heaven is now one family, yet Yunnan alone has not accepted the official calendar and has killed my envoys—can you be my Lu Jia?”
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the eighth year of Hongwu, when the Founder deliberated sending envoys again to persuade the Prince of Liang, he summoned Yun and said to him, “Under Heaven is now one family, yet Yunnan alone has not accepted the official calendar and has killed my envoys—can you be my Lu Jia?”

sentences.zh: 雲頓首請行。

translations.literal: Yun bowed his head and asked to go.
translations.idiomatic: Yun bowed his head and asked to go.

sentences.zh: 時梁王遣鐵知院輩二十余人使漠北，為大將軍所獲，送京師，太祖釋之，令與雲偕行。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Liang had sent Tie Zhuyuan and more than twenty others as envoys to the northern desert; they were captured by the grand general, sent to the capital, released by the Founder, and ordered to travel together with Yun.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Prince of Liang had sent Tie Zhuyuan and more than twenty others as envoys to the northern desert; they were captured by the grand general, sent to the capital, released by the Founder, and ordered to travel together with Yun.

sentences.zh: 既入境，鐵知院等謀曰：「吾輩奉使被執，罪且死。」

translations.literal: Once they had entered the territory, Tie Zhuyuan and the others plotted, saying: We were sent on mission and were captured—our crime warrants death.”
translations.idiomatic: Once they had entered the territory, Tie Zhuyuan and the others plotted, saying, “We were sent on mission and were captured—our crime warrants death.”

sentences.zh: 乃誘雲，令詐為元使，改制書，共紿梁王。

translations.literal: They then deceived Yun, making him falsely pose as a Yuan envoy, altered the imperial rescript, and together duped the Prince of Liang.
translations.idiomatic: They then deceived Yun, making him falsely pose as a Yuan envoy, altered the imperial rescript, and together duped the Prince of Liang.

sentences.zh: 雲誓死不從，鐵知院等遂殺雲。

translations.literal: Yun swore he would rather die than comply; Tie Zhuyuan and the others then killed Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Yun swore he would rather die than comply; Tie Zhuyuan and the others then killed Yun.

sentences.zh: 梁王聞其事，收雲骨，送蜀給孤寺殯之。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Liang learned of the affair, he gathered Yun's bones and sent them to the Jigu Temple in Shu for burial.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Liang learned of the affair, he gathered Yun's bones and sent them to the Jigu Temple in Shu for burial.

sentences.zh: 雲子黻，上雲事於朝。

translations.literal: Yun's son Fu reported Yun's case to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Yun's son Fu reported Yun's case to the court.

sentences.zh: 詔馳傳返葬，以黻為國子生。

translations.literal: An edict ordered rapid courier return for burial, and Fu was made a student of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered rapid courier return for burial, and Fu was made a student of the National University.

sentences.zh: 弘治四年五月贈雲刑部尚書，謚忠節，與祎並祠，改祠額曰二忠。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the fourth year of Hongzhi, Yun was posthumously granted Minister of Justice and the posthumous title Zhongjie (Loyal Integrity); he was enshrined together with Yi, and the temple inscription was changed to Two Loyal Ones.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the fourth year of Hongzhi, Yun was posthumously granted Minister of Justice and the posthumous title Zhongjie (Loyal Integrity); he was enshrined together with Yi, and the temple inscription was changed to "Two Loyal Ones."

sentences.zh: 熊鼎，字伯潁，臨川人。

translations.literal: Xiong Ding, styled Boying, was a native of Linchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Ding, styled Boying, was a native of Linchuan.

sentences.zh: 元末舉於鄉，長龍溪書院。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yuan he passed the provincial examination and was head of Longxi Academy.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuan he passed the provincial examination and was head of Longxi Academy.

sentences.zh: 江西寇亂，鼎結鄉兵自守。

translations.literal: When Jiangxi was disturbed by bandits, Ding organized local militia for self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangxi was disturbed by bandits, Ding organized local militia for self-defense.

sentences.zh: 陳友諒屢脅之，不應。

translations.literal: Chen Youliang repeatedly coerced him, but he would not respond.
