translations.idiomatic: Chen Youliang repeatedly coerced him, but he would not respond.

sentences.zh: 鄧愈鎮江西，數延見，奇其才，薦之。

translations.literal: When Deng Yu governed Jiangxi, he repeatedly summoned Ding, marveled at his talent, and recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: When Deng Yu governed Jiangxi, he repeatedly summoned Ding, marveled at his talent, and recommended him.

sentences.zh: 太祖欲官之，以親老辭，乃留愈幕府贊軍事。

translations.literal: The Founder wished to grant him office, but he declined citing aged parents and remained in Yu's staff to assist in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The Founder wished to grant him office, but he declined citing aged parents and remained in Yu's staff to assist in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 母喪除，召至京師，授德清縣丞。

translations.literal: After mourning for his mother was completed, he was summoned to the capital and appointed Assistant Magistrate of Deqing County.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning for his mother was completed, he was summoned to the capital and appointed Assistant Magistrate of Deqing County.

sentences.zh: 松江民錢鶴臯反，鄰郡大驚，鼎鎮之以靜。

translations.literal: When the Songjiang commoner Qian He'gao rebelled, neighboring prefectures were greatly alarmed; Ding kept the region calm.
translations.idiomatic: When the Songjiang commoner Qian He'gao rebelled, neighboring prefectures were greatly alarmed; Ding kept the region calm.

sentences.zh: 吳元年召議禮儀，除中書考功博士。

translations.literal: In the Wu era he was summoned to discuss ritual, and appointed Doctor of Performance Evaluation in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wu era he was summoned to discuss ritual, and appointed Doctor of Performance Evaluation in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 遷起居註，承詔搜括故事可懲戒者，書新宮壁間。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Diarist; by imperial order he gathered historical precedents that could serve as warnings and wrote them on the walls of the new palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Diarist; by imperial order he gathered historical precedents that could serve as warnings and wrote them on the walls of the new palace.

sentences.zh: 舍人耿忠使廣信還，奏郡縣官違法狀，帝遣御史廉之。

translations.literal: Secretariat Gentleman Geng Zhong returned from mission to Guangxin and memorialized on violations by prefectural and county officials; the emperor dispatched censors to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Secretariat Gentleman Geng Zhong returned from mission to Guangxin and memorialized on violations by prefectural and county officials; the emperor dispatched censors to investigate.

sentences.zh: 而時已頒赦書，丞相李善長再諫不納，鼎偕給事中尹正進曰：「朝廷布大信於四方，復以細故煩御史，失信，且褻威。」

translations.literal: But by then an amnesty had already been promulgated; Chancellor Li Shanchang remonstrated twice without success. Ding together with Supervising Secretary Yin Zheng advanced and said: The court has spread great trust throughout the realm—to trouble censors again over trivial matters breaks faith and moreover debases authority.”
translations.idiomatic: But by then an amnesty had already been promulgated; Chancellor Li Shanchang remonstrated twice without success. Ding together with Supervising Secretary Yin Zheng advanced and said, “The court has spread great trust throughout the realm—to trouble censors again over trivial matters breaks faith and moreover debases authority.”

sentences.zh: 帝默然久之，乃不遣物史。

translations.literal: The emperor was silent for a long time, and in the end did not dispatch the censors.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was silent for a long time, and in the end did not dispatch the censors.

sentences.zh: 洪武改元，新設浙江按察司，以鼎為僉事，分部臺、溫。

translations.literal: At the change of reign title to Hongwu, when the Zhejiang Surveillance Commission was newly established, Ding was made Vice Commissioner, administering Taizhou and Wenzhou circuits.
translations.idiomatic: At the change of reign title to Hongwu, when the Zhejiang Surveillance Commission was newly established, Ding was made Vice Commissioner, administering Taizhou and Wenzhou circuits.

sentences.zh: 臺、溫自方氏竊據，偽官捍將二百人，暴橫甚。

translations.literal: Taizhou and Wenzhou, since they had been seized by the Fang clan, had some two hundred false officials and obstinate generals who were exceedingly violent and overbearing.
translations.idiomatic: Taizhou and Wenzhou, since they had been seized by the Fang clan, had some two hundred false officials and obstinate generals who were exceedingly violent and overbearing.

sentences.zh: 鼎盡遷之江、淮間，民始安。

translations.literal: Ding relocated them all to the region between the Yangzi and Huai rivers, and only then did the people find peace.
translations.idiomatic: Ding had them all relocated to the Jiang-Huai region, and only then did the people at last find peace.

sentences.zh: 平陽知州梅鎰坐贓，辨不已，民數百鹹訴知州無罪。

translations.literal: Mei Yi, Prefect of Pingyang, was charged with corruption; he argued incessantly in his own defense, and several hundred commoners all petitioned that the prefect was innocent.
translations.idiomatic: Mei Yi, the prefect of Pingyang, stood accused of corruption. He protested his innocence without cease, and several hundred commoners petitioned as one that their prefect was guiltless.

sentences.zh: 鼎將聽之，吏白鼎：「釋知州，如故出何？」

translations.literal: Ding was about to hear the case when a clerk told Ding: If we release the prefect, what excuse can we give for how he walked out as before?”
translations.idiomatic: Ding was about to hear the case when a clerk warned him, "If we release the prefect, what excuse can we offer for letting him walk out as before?"

sentences.zh: 鼎嘆曰：「法以誅罪，吾敢畏譴，誅無罪人乎！」

translations.literal: Ding sighed and said: The law is for punishing crime—how dare I fear censure and execute an innocent man!”
translations.idiomatic: Ding sighed and said, "The law exists to punish the guilty—am I to fear reprimand and put an innocent man to death?"

sentences.zh: 釋鎰，以情聞，報如其奏。

translations.literal: He released Mei Yi, reported the circumstances to the throne, and the reply matched his memorial.
translations.idiomatic: He released Mei Yi, reported the full circumstances to the throne, and the imperial reply accorded with his memorial.

sentences.zh: 寧海民陳德仲支解黎異，異妻屢訴不得直。

translations.literal: The Ninghai commoner Chen Dezhong dismembered Li Yi; Yi's wife repeatedly petitioned but could not obtain justice.
translations.idiomatic: In Ninghai, Chen Dezhong had dismembered Li Yi, and Yi's wife petitioned again and again without ever obtaining justice.

sentences.zh: 鼎一日覽牒，有青蛙立案上，鼎曰：「蛙非黎異乎？

translations.literal: One day as Ding was reviewing documents, a green frog appeared on the case folder. Ding said: Is this frog not Li Yi?
translations.idiomatic: One day while Ding was reviewing case papers, a green frog appeared on the dossier before him. Ding said, "Is this frog not Li Yi?

sentences.zh: 果異，止勿動。」

translations.literal: It truly was Yi; he ordered that it not be disturbed.”
translations.idiomatic: It was indeed Yi, and he ordered that the frog not be touched."

sentences.zh: 蛙果勿動，乃逮德仲，鞫實，立正其罪。

translations.literal: The frog indeed did not move. Then he arrested Dezhong, examined the facts, and immediately executed him for his crime.
translations.idiomatic: The frog truly did not stir. Ding then arrested Dezhong, established the facts under interrogation, and at once executed him for the crime.

sentences.zh: 是秋，山東初定，設按察司，復以鼎為僉事。

translations.literal: That autumn, Shandong was newly pacified; a Surveillance Commission was established, and Ding was again made Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn, with Shandong newly pacified, a Surveillance Commission was established and Ding was again appointed Vice Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 鼎至，奏罷不職有司數十輩，列部肅清。

translations.literal: When Ding arrived, he memorialized to dismiss several dozen negligent officials, and the whole department was cleansed.
translations.idiomatic: When Ding arrived, he memorialized for the dismissal of several dozen derelict officials, and the entire commission was brought to order.

sentences.zh: 鼎欲稽官吏利弊，乃令郡縣各置二歷，日書所治訟獄錢粟事，一留郡縣，一上憲府，遞更易，按歷鉤考之，莫敢隱者。

translations.literal: Ding wished to audit officials' gains and losses, so he ordered each prefecture and county to keep two ledgers, daily recording lawsuits, prisons, money, and grain handled—one kept locally, one sent up to the surveillance office, rotated in turn and checked against each other; none dared conceal anything.
translations.idiomatic: Seeking to audit what officials gained and lost in office, Ding ordered every prefecture and county to maintain two ledgers, recording daily all lawsuits, prisons, money, and grain under their charge—one kept locally and one sent to the surveillance office, exchanged in rotation and cross-checked. None dared conceal anything.

sentences.zh: 尋進副使，徙晉王府右傅。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Assistant Commissioner and transferred to Right Tutor of the Prince of Jin's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Assistant Commissioner and transferred to serve as Right Tutor in the household of the Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 坐累左遷，復授王府參軍，召為刑部主事。

translations.literal: Through implication in a case he was demoted, again granted the post of Military Adjutant in the princely establishment, then summoned as Chief Clerk of the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Implicated in a case, he was demoted, then reappointed Military Adjutant in the princely household before being summoned to serve as Chief Clerk in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 八年，西部朵兒只班率部落內附，改鼎岐寧衛經歷。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Dordji Baan of the western tribes led his people to submit; Ding was reassigned as Clerk of Qining Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, when Dordji Baan of the western tribes led his people to submit, Ding was reassigned as clerk of Qining Guard.

sentences.zh: 既至，知寇偽降，密疏論之。

translations.literal: Once there, knowing the bandits had falsely surrendered, he sent a secret memorial arguing this.
translations.idiomatic: Once he arrived, recognizing that the bandits had feigned surrender, he sent a secret memorial arguing the point.

sentences.zh: 帝遣使慰勞，賜裘帽，復遣中使趙成召鼎。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys to comfort and reward him with fur coat and cap, and again sent the palace envoy Zhao Cheng to summon Ding.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys to comfort him, bestowed a fur coat and cap, and again dispatched the palace envoy Zhao Cheng to summon Ding.

sentences.zh: 鼎既行，寇果叛，脅鼎北還。

translations.literal: After Ding set out, the bandits indeed rebelled and forced Ding to return north.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had Ding set out when the bandits rebelled as he had warned, forcing him to turn back north.

sentences.zh: 鼎責以大義，罵之，遂與成及知事杜寅俱被殺。

translations.literal: Ding rebuked them with righteous principle and cursed them; he was then killed together with Cheng and the clerk Du Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Ding rebuked them in the name of righteousness and cursed them to their faces; he was killed together with Cheng and the clerk Du Yin.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，悼惜，命葬之黃羊川，立祠，以所食俸給其家。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he mourned and lamented, ordered burial at Huangyangchuan, erected a shrine, and granted his salary allotment to his family.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it, he mourned his loss and ordered Ding buried at Huangyangchuan, a shrine erected in his honor, and his salary allotment granted to his family.

sentences.zh: 易紹宗，攸人。

translations.literal: Yi Shaozong, a native of You County.
translations.idiomatic: Yi Shaozong was a native of You County.

sentences.zh: 洪武時，從軍有功，授象山縣錢倉所千戶。

translations.literal: During the Hongwu era he followed the army with merit and was granted the post of Thousand-Commander at Qiancang Guard in Xiangshan County.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongwu reign he campaigned with distinction and was appointed Thousand-Commander at Qiancang Guard in Xiangshan County.

sentences.zh: 建文三年，倭登岸剽掠。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianwen, Japanese pirates came ashore to plunder.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Jianwen reign, Japanese pirates came ashore to raid and plunder.

sentences.zh: 紹宗大書於壁曰：「設將禦敵，設軍衛民。

translations.literal: Shaozong wrote large characters on the wall, saying: Appoint generals to repel the enemy; maintain armies to protect the people.
translations.idiomatic: Shaozong wrote in large characters on the wall, "Appoint generals to repel the enemy; maintain armies to protect the people.

sentences.zh: 縱敵不忠。

translations.literal: To let the enemy go is disloyalty.
translations.idiomatic: To let the enemy go is disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 棄民不仁。

translations.literal: To abandon the people is inhumanity.
translations.idiomatic: To abandon the people is inhumanity.

sentences.zh: 不忠不仁，何以為臣！

translations.literal: Without loyalty and humanity, how can one be a minister!
translations.idiomatic: Without loyalty and humanity, how can one be a minister!

sentences.zh: 為臣不職，何以為人！」

translations.literal: As a minister who fails his duty, how can one be called human!”
translations.idiomatic: As a minister who fails in his duty, how can one still be called human!"

sentences.zh: 書畢，命妻李具牲酒生奠之，訣而出，密令遊兵間道焚賊舟。

translations.literal: When he had finished writing, he ordered his wife Li to prepare sacrificial meat and wine and offer them while he was still alive, bid farewell and went out, and secretly ordered roving soldiers by a hidden path to burn the pirates' boats.
translations.idiomatic: When he had finished writing, he told his wife Li to prepare meat and wine for a living farewell offering, took his leave, and secretly ordered roving troops by a hidden route to burn the pirates' boats.

sentences.zh: 賊驚救，紹宗格戰，追至海岸，陷淖中，手刃數十賊，遂被害。

translations.literal: The pirates rushed to save their boats; Shaozong fought hand to hand, pursued them to the seashore, sank into mud, killed dozens of pirates with his own hand, and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: The pirates rushed to save their boats. Shaozong fought them hand to hand, pursued them to the shore, sank into the mud, and with his own blade cut down dozens of them before he was killed.

sentences.zh: 其妻攜孤奏於朝，賜葬祭，勒碑旌之。

translations.literal: His wife brought their orphan to petition the court; burial sacrifices were granted and a stele erected to honor him.
translations.idiomatic: His wife brought their orphan before the throne to petition the court; the court granted burial rites and had a stele erected in his honor.

sentences.zh: 琴彭，交阯人。

translations.literal: Qin Peng, a native of Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Peng was a native of Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 永樂中，以乂安知府署茶籠州事，有善政。

translations.literal: During the Yongle reign, as prefect of Yian he acted in the affairs of Chalong Prefecture and had benevolent governance.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongle reign, as prefect of Yian he acted in the affairs of Chalong Prefecture and governed with benevolence.

sentences.zh: 宣德元年，黎利反，率眾圍其城。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuande, Le Loi rebelled and led a host to besiege the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Xuande reign, Le Loi rebelled and led a host to besiege the city.

sentences.zh: 彭拒守七月，糧盡卒疲，諸將無援者，巡按御史飛章請救。

translations.literal: Peng held out for seven months; grain was exhausted and the troops worn out, with no generals coming to relieve him; the touring censor submitted urgent memorials seeking rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Peng held out for seven months; grain ran out and his troops were exhausted, with no generals coming to his relief, and the touring censor sent urgent memorials seeking rescue.

sentences.zh: 宣宗馳敕責榮昌伯陳智等曰：「茶籠守彭被困孤城，矢死無貳，若等不援，將何以逃責！

translations.literal: The Xuande Emperor urgently sent an edict rebuking the Earl of Rongchang, Chen Zhi, and others, saying: "Chalong's defender Peng is trapped in an isolated city, resolute unto death and without duplicity—if you do not go to his aid, how will you escape responsibility!
translations.idiomatic: The Xuande Emperor urgently sent an edict rebuking the Earl of Rongchang, Chen Zhi, and others, saying, "Chalong's defender Peng is trapped in an isolated city, resolute unto death and without duplicity—if you do not go to his aid, how will you escape responsibility!

sentences.zh: 急發兵解圍，無幹國憲。」

translations.literal: Send troops at once to relieve the siege; do not offend against the laws of the state."
translations.idiomatic: Send troops at once to relieve the siege; do not offend against the laws of the state."

sentences.zh: 敕未至而城陷，彭死之。

translations.literal: Before the edict arrived the city fell, and Peng died in its defense.
translations.idiomatic: Before the edict arrived the city fell, and Peng died in its defense.

sentences.zh: 詔贈交阯左布政使，送一子京師官之。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously made him Left Administrative Commissioner of Jiaozhi and had one son sent to the capital for appointment to office.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made him Left Administrative Commissioner of Jiaozhi and had one son sent to the capital for appointment to office.

sentences.zh: 時交阯人陳汝石、朱多蒲、陶季容、陳汀亦皆以忠節著。

translations.literal: At the time Chen Rushi, Zhu Duopu, Tao Jirong, and Chen Ting of Jiaozhi were also known for loyalty and integrity.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Chen Rushi, Zhu Duopu, Tao Jirong, and Chen Ting of Jiaozhi were likewise famed for loyalty and steadfast integrity.

sentences.zh: 汝石初為陳氏小校，大軍南征，率先歸附，積功至都指揮僉事。

translations.literal: Rushi was originally a minor officer of the Chen clan; when the great army marched south he was first to submit, accumulating merit until he reached Vice Commissioner of Chief Military Command.
translations.idiomatic: Rushi had begun as a minor officer under the Chen regime; when the imperial army marched south he was among the first to submit, rising through merit to Vice Commissioner of Chief Military Command.

sentences.zh: 永樂十七年，四忙士官車綿子等叛。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year of Yongle, the Si Mang official Che Mianzi and others rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year of the Yongle reign, Che Mianzi, an official of Si Mang, and others rose in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 汝石從方政討之，深入賊陣，中流矢墜馬，與千戶朱多蒲皆死。

translations.literal: Rushi followed Fang Zheng to suppress them, penetrated deep into the rebel ranks, was struck by an arrow and fell from his horse; he and Thousand-Commander Zhu Duopu both died.
translations.idiomatic: Rushi followed Fang Zheng to suppress the rebels, plunged deep into their ranks, was struck by an arrow and thrown from his horse, and died together with Thousand-Commander Zhu Duopu.

sentences.zh: 多蒲，亦交阯人。

translations.literal: Duopu was also a native of Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Duopu, too, was a native of Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 事聞，遣行人賜祭，賻其家，官為置冢。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, an envoy was sent with sacrificial offerings, compensation was given to their families, and the government built tombs for them.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the court, an envoy was dispatched with sacrificial offerings, compensation was granted to their families, and the state built tombs for them.

sentences.zh: 皇甫斌，壽州人。

translations.literal: Huangfu Bin, a native of Shouzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Bin was a native of Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 先為興州右屯衛指揮同知，以才調遼海衛。

translations.literal: He had first been Deputy Commander of Xingzhou Right Garrison and was transferred to Liaohai Guard for his talent.
translations.idiomatic: He had first served as Deputy Commander of the Xingzhou Right Garrison and was transferred to Liaohai Guard on account of his ability.

sentences.zh: 忠勇有智略，遇警，輒身先士卒。

translations.literal: Loyal and brave with strategic insight; whenever alarm arose he always led from the front.
translations.idiomatic: Loyal, brave, and resourceful, he always placed himself at the head of his men whenever danger arose.

sentences.zh: 宣德五年十月勒兵禦寇，至密城東峪，自旦及晡力戰，矢盡援絕，子弼以身衛父，俱戰死。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fifth year of Xuande he drilled troops against bandits and reached Miyu east of Micheng; from dawn till afternoon they fought desperately, arrows exhausted and reinforcements cut off; his son Bi shielded his father with his body and both died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fifth year of Xuande he mustered troops against bandits and fought at Miyu east of Micheng from dawn until evening; when arrows were spent and relief failed to come, his son Bi shielded him with his own body, and both fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 千戶吳貴，百戶吳襄、毛觀並驍勇，出必沖鋒，至是皆死。

translations.literal: Thousand-Commander Wu Gui and Centurions Wu Xiang and Mao Guan were all fiercely brave and always charged the vanguard when they went out; on this occasion they all died.
translations.idiomatic: Thousand-Commander Wu Gui and Centurions Wu Xiang and Mao Guan were all fiercely brave men who invariably led the charge; on this day they all perished.

sentences.zh: 斌等雖死，殺傷過當，寇亦引退。

translations.literal: Though Bin and the others died, they killed disproportionately many enemies and the bandits also withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Though Bin and his companions died, they inflicted losses far beyond their own, and the bandits withdrew as well.

sentences.zh: 事聞，詔有司褒恤。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, an edict ordered the responsible offices to honor and compensate them.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the throne, an edict ordered the responsible offices to honor and compensate them.

sentences.zh: 張瑛，字彥華，浙江建德人。

translations.literal: Zhang Ying, courtesy name Yanhua, a native of Jiande in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ying, styled Yanhua, was a native of Jiande in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 永樂中，舉於鄉，歷刑部員外郎。

translations.literal: During Yongle he passed the provincial examination and served as Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongle reign he passed the provincial examination and served as Vice Director in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 正統時，擢建寧知府。

translations.literal: During Zhengtong he was promoted to Prefect of Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengtong era he was promoted to prefect of Jianning.

sentences.zh: 鄧茂七作亂，賊二千余迫城結砦，四出剽掠。

translations.literal: Deng Maoqi rebelled; over two thousand bandits pressed on the city and built stockades, raiding in all directions.
translations.idiomatic: When Deng Maoqi rebelled, more than two thousand bandits pressed upon the city, built stockades, and fanned out to plunder on every side.

sentences.zh: 瑛率建安典史鄭烈會都指揮徐信軍，分三路襲之，斬首五百余，遂拔其砦。

translations.literal: Ying led Jian'an Record Clerk Zheng Lie to join Military Commander Xu Xin's army, attacking in three columns; over five hundred heads were taken and the stockade was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Ying led Jian'an Record Clerk Zheng Lie to join the army of Military Commander Xu Xin, struck in three columns, took more than five hundred heads, and captured the stockade.

sentences.zh: 進右參議，仍知府事。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Assistant Administration Commissioner and still handled prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Assistant Administration Commissioner while continuing to govern the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 烈亦遷主簿。

translations.literal: Lie was also transferred to Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Lie was promoted to chief clerk as well.

sentences.zh: 茂七既誅，其黨林拾得等轉掠城下，瑛與從父敬禦之。

translations.literal: After Maoqi was executed, his followers Lin Shide and others turned to plunder below the city walls; Ying and his uncle Jing resisted them.
translations.idiomatic: After Maoqi was put to death, his followers Lin Shide and others raided beneath the city walls; Ying and his uncle Jing went out to resist them.

sentences.zh: 賊敗，乘勝逐北，陷伏中，敬死，瑛被執，大罵不屈死。

translations.literal: The bandits were defeated; pursuing victory northward they fell into an ambush; Jing died, Ying was captured, cursed them without yielding, and died.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits were routed, but in the pursuit Ying and his men fell into an ambush; Jing was killed, Ying was captured, cursed his captors without yielding, and died.

sentences.zh: 詔贈福建按察使，賜祭，官其子。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously granted him Surveillance Commissioner of Fujian, bestowed sacrificial offerings, and granted office to his son.
translations.idiomatic: An edict posthumously made him Surveillance Commissioner of Fujian, granted sacrificial honors, and enrolled his son in office.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，建寧知府劉玙請於朝，立祠致祭。

translations.literal: During Hongzhi, Jianning Prefect Liu Yu petitioned the court to erect a shrine and offer sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongzhi reign, Jianning Prefect Liu Yu petitioned the court to erect a shrine and perform regular sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 時泉州守熊尚初亦以拒賊被執死。

translations.literal: At the time Quanzhou Prefect Xiong Shangchu also died captured while resisting bandits.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time Xiong Shangchu, prefect of Quanzhou, also died in captivity after resisting bandits.

sentences.zh: 尚初，南昌人。

translations.literal: Shangchu, a native of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Shangchu was a native of Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 初為吏，以才擢都察院都事，進經歷。

translations.literal: He had begun as a clerk, was promoted for talent to Secretariat Officer of the Censorate, and advanced to Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He had begun as a clerk, was promoted for ability to Secretariat Officer of the Censorate, and later advanced to clerk.

sentences.zh: 正統中，用都御史陳鎰薦，擢泉州知府。

translations.literal: During Zhengtong, on recommendation of Censor-in-Chief Chen Yong he was promoted to Prefect of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengtong reign, on the recommendation of Censor-in-Chief Chen Yong, he was promoted to prefect of Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 盜起，上官檄尚初監軍，不旬日降賊數百。

translations.literal: Bandits arose; his superiors ordered Shangchu to supervise the army, and within ten days several hundred bandits surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose, his superiors ordered Shangchu to take command of the troops, and within ten days several hundred bandits surrendered.

sentences.zh: 已而賊逼城下，守將不敢禦。

translations.literal: Before long the bandits pressed on the city; the garrison commander dared not resist.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the bandits pressed upon the city, yet the garrison commander dared not meet them.

sentences.zh: 尚初憤，提民兵數百，與晉江主簿史孟常、陰陽訓術楊仕弘分統之，拒於古陵坡。

translations.literal: Shangchu was furious; he led several hundred militia, dividing command with Jinjiang Chief Clerk Shi Mengchang and Yin-Yang Instructor Yang Shihong, and resisted at Guling Slope.
translations.idiomatic: Furious, Shangchu raised several hundred militia, divided command with Jinjiang Chief Clerk Shi Mengchang and Yin-Yang Instructor Yang Shihong, and met the bandits at Guling Slope.

sentences.zh: 兵敗，皆遇害。

translations.literal: The army was defeated; all were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Their force was defeated, and all were killed.

sentences.zh: 郡人哀之，為配享忠臣廟。

translations.literal: The people of the prefecture mourned them and enshrined them as associate sacrifices in the Shrine of Loyal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the prefecture mourned them and installed them as associate spirits in the Shrine of Loyal Ministers.

sentences.zh: 王禎，字維禎，吉水人。

translations.literal: Wang Zhen, courtesy name Weizhen, a native of Jishui.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen, styled Weizhen, was a native of Jishui.

sentences.zh: 祖省，死建文難，自有傳。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sheng died in the Jianwen troubles; he has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sheng had died in the troubles of the Jianwen reign; he has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 成化初，禎由國子生授夔州通判。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Chenghua, Zhen was appointed Vice Prefect of Kuizhou from Imperial Academy student status.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Chenghua reign, Zhen was appointed vice prefect of Kuizhou after graduating from the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 二年，荊、襄石和尚流劫至巫山，督盜同知王某者怯不救。

translations.literal: In the second year, bandits from Jing-Xiang—the Stone Monk—flowed to plunder as far as Wushan; the Patrol Bandit Vice Prefect surnamed Wang was cowardly and would not rescue.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, the Stone Monk and his band from Jing and Xiang swept as far as Wushan to plunder; the Vice Prefect in charge of bandit suppression, a man surnamed Wang, was too timid to go to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 禎面數之，即代勒所部民兵，晝夜行。

translations.literal: Zhen rebuked him to his face, then took his place to drill the militia under his command, marching day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen rebuked him to his face, then took command himself, drilling the militia under his charge and marching day and night.

sentences.zh: 至則城已陷，賊方聚山中。

translations.literal: When they arrived the city had already fallen; the bandits were gathered in the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived, the city had already fallen and the bandits were massed in the hills.

sentences.zh: 禎擊殺其魁，余盡遁，乃行縣撫傷殘，招潰散，久乃得還。

translations.literal: Zhen killed their leader; the rest all fled; then he traveled through the counties comforting the wounded and destitute, recruiting scattered troops; only after a long time was he able to return.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen struck down their leader and the rest fled; he then traveled through the counties to succor the wounded and destitute and gather up scattered troops, and only after a long while was he able to return.

sentences.zh: 甫三日，賊復劫大昌。

translations.literal: Barely three days later, bandits again raided Dachang.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly three days had passed when the bandits raided Dachang again.

sentences.zh: 禎趣同知行，不應。

translations.literal: Zhen urged the Vice Prefect to march; he did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen urged the Vice Prefect to march, but received no answer.

sentences.zh: 指揮曹能、柴成與同知比，激禎曰：「公為國出力，肯復行乎？」

translations.literal: Commanders Cao Neng and Chai Cheng, together with the Vice Prefect, goaded Zhen, saying: You exert yourself for the state—are you willing to go again?”
translations.idiomatic: Commanders Cao Neng and Chai Cheng, siding with the Vice Prefect, goaded Zhen, saying, "You exert yourself for the state—are you willing to go again?"

sentences.zh: 禎即請往，兩人偽許相左右。

translations.literal: Zhen immediately asked to go; the two men falsely promised to stand by him on either side.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen at once volunteered to go; the two men falsely promised to stand by him on either flank.

sentences.zh: 禎上馬，挾二人與俱，夾水陣。

translations.literal: Zhen mounted his horse, taking the two men with him, and formed battle lines on either side of the water.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen mounted, taking the two men with him, and drew up his force on either bank of the stream.

sentences.zh: 既渡，兩人見賊即走。

translations.literal: Once they had crossed, the two men saw the bandits and fled at once.
translations.idiomatic: Once they had crossed, the two men caught sight of the bandits and fled at once.

sentences.zh: 禎被圍半日，誤入淖中，賊執欲降之，禎大罵。

translations.literal: Zhen was surrounded for half a day, mistakenly entered a marsh, was captured and the bandits wished to make him surrender; Zhen cursed them loudly.
translations.idiomatic: Surrounded for half a day, Zhen blundered into a marsh, was seized, and when the bandits tried to force his surrender he cursed them loudly.

sentences.zh: 賊怒，斷其喉及右臂而死。

translations.literal: The bandits were enraged and cut his throat and right arm, killing him.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the bandits cut his throat and right arm and killed him.

sentences.zh: 從行者奉節典史及部卒六百余人皆死。

translations.literal: Those who had accompanied him—the Protocol Clerk and over six hundred soldiers—all died.
translations.idiomatic: All who had accompanied him—the Protocol Clerk and more than six hundred soldiers—died as well.

sentences.zh: 自死所至府三百余裏，所乘馬奔歸，血淋漓，毛盡赤。

translations.literal: From the place of death to the prefectural seat was over three hundred li; the horse he had ridden galloped back, blood dripping everywhere, its hair entirely red.
translations.idiomatic: From the place where he died to the prefectural seat was more than three hundred li; the horse he had ridden galloped home drenched in blood, its coat entirely red.

sentences.zh: 眾始知禎敗，往覓屍，面如生。

translations.literal: Only then did the people learn Zhen had been defeated; they went to seek his corpse; his face was as if alive.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did the people learn of Zhen's defeat; they went to recover his body, and his face looked as if he were still alive.

sentences.zh: 子廣鬻馬為歸貲，王同知得馬不償直。

translations.literal: His son Guang sold the horse for travel funds for the return journey; Vice Prefect Wang got the horse but did not pay its full price.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guang sold the horse to pay for bringing the body home; Vice Prefect Wang took the horse but never paid its full worth.

sentences.zh: 櫬既行，馬夜半哀鳴。

translations.literal: After the coffin had departed, at midnight the horse wailed mournfully.
translations.idiomatic: After the coffin had set out, the horse wailed mournfully at midnight.

sentences.zh: 同知起視之，馬驟前嚙項，搗其胸，翼日嘔血死，人稱為義馬。

translations.literal: The Vice Prefect rose to look; the horse suddenly rushed forward, bit his neck, struck his chest; the next day he vomited blood and died; people called it the Righteous Horse.
translations.idiomatic: The Vice Prefect rose to look, and the horse suddenly charged forward, bit his neck, and struck his chest; the next day he vomited blood and died, and people called it the Righteous Horse.

sentences.zh: 事聞，贈禎僉事，錄一子。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, Zhen was posthumously granted Vice Commissioner rank and one son was enrolled in office.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached the throne, Zhen was posthumously granted the rank of Vice Commissioner and one son was enrolled in office.

sentences.zh: 萬琛，字廷獻，宣城人。

translations.literal: Wan Chen, courtesy name Tingxian, a native of Xuancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wan Chen, styled Tingxian, was a native of Xuancheng.

sentences.zh: 慷慨負氣節，舉於鄉。

translations.literal: Magnanimous and possessed of moral integrity; he passed the provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: Generous in spirit and firm in integrity, he passed the provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，知瑞金縣。

translations.literal: During Hongzhi he served as Magistrate of Ruijin County.
translations.idiomatic: During the Hongzhi reign he served as magistrate of Ruijin County.

sentences.zh: 十八年正月，劇盜大至，縣人洶洶逃竄。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighteenth year, fierce bandits arrived in great numbers; the county people fled in panic.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eighteenth year, fierce bandits descended in force and the people of the county fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 有勸琛急去者，琛斥之，率民兵數十人迎敵，殺賊二十余人。

translations.literal: Some urged Chen to flee quickly; he rebuked them, led several dozen militia to meet the enemy, and killed over twenty bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When some urged Chen to flee at once, he rebuked them, led several dozen militiamen to meet the enemy, and killed more than twenty bandits.

sentences.zh: 相持至明日，力屈被執，罵不絕口，賊攢刺之，乃死。

translations.literal: The contest lasted until the next day; strength exhausted he was captured, cursed without pause; the bandits stabbed him repeatedly and he died.
translations.idiomatic: The fight lasted until the next day; when his strength failed he was captured and cursed them without cease until the bandits stabbed him again and again and he died.

sentences.zh: 贈光祿少卿，賜祭葬，予蔭。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, bestowed sacrificial burial, and hereditary privilege was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, granted state burial rites, and his family received hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 時有王祐者，為廣昌知縣，賊至，民盡逃，援兵又不至。

translations.literal: At the time there was Wang You, Magistrate of Guangchang County; when bandits arrived the people all fled and reinforcements did not come.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there was Wang You, magistrate of Guangchang County; when bandits arrived the people all fled and no reinforcements came.

sentences.zh: 祐拔刀自刲其腹曰：「有城不能守，何生為！」

translations.literal: You drew his sword and cut his own belly, saying: Having a city yet unable to defend it—what is life for!”
translations.idiomatic: You drew his sword and cut open his own belly, crying, "With a city to defend and unable to hold it—what is life worth?"

sentences.zh: 左右奔奪其刀。

translations.literal: Those around him rushed to wrest away his sword.
translations.idiomatic: Those around him rushed forward and wrested the sword from his hand.

sentences.zh: 後援兵集，賊稍退。

translations.literal: Later reinforcements gathered and the bandits retreated somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when reinforcements gathered, the bandits withdrew somewhat.

sentences.zh: 越七日復突至，祐倉皇赴敵，死之。

translations.literal: Seven days later they suddenly returned; You rushed in haste to meet the enemy and died.
translations.idiomatic: Seven days later the bandits struck again; You rushed out in haste to meet them and was killed.

sentences.zh: 周憲，安陸人。

translations.literal: Zhou Xian, a native of Anlu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Xian was a native of Anlu.

sentences.zh: 弘治六年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the sixth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the sixth year of the Hongzhi reign.

sentences.zh: 除刑部主事，進員外郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Secretary in the Ministry of Justice and promoted to Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed a secretary in the Ministry of Justice and promoted to vice director.

sentences.zh: 十七年坐事下詔獄，謫袞州通判。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, because of an affair he was sent to the imperial prison by edict and demoted to Associate Prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was imprisoned by imperial order on account of misconduct and demoted to associate prefect of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 正德初，復故官，歷江西副使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhengde reign, he was restored to his former office and served as Vice Commissioner of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: At the outset of the Zhengde reign he was restored to his former rank and served as vice commissioner of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 華林、馬腦賊方熾，總督陳金檄憲剿之，平馬腦砦及仙女、雞公嶺諸寨，先後斬獲千余人。

translations.literal: The Hualin and Manao bandits were then raging; Grand Coordinator Chen Jin ordered Xian to suppress them, and he pacified the Manao stockade and the stockades at Xiannü and Jigong Ridge, beheading and capturing more than a thousand men in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The Hualin and Manao bandits were then at their fiercest. Grand Coordinator Chen Jin ordered Xian to suppress them; he pacified the Manao stockade and the stockades at Xiannü and Jigong Ridge, killing or capturing more than a thousand men in the course of the campaign.

sentences.zh: 華林賊窘，遣諜者詭言饑困狀。

translations.literal: The Hualin bandits, hard pressed, sent a spy to deceive with talk of hunger and distress.
translations.idiomatic: The Hualin bandits, now hard pressed, sent a spy to spread false reports of hunger and exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 憲信之，移檄會師夾擊。

translations.literal: Xian believed it and issued a dispatch calling on the armies to unite and attack from both sides.
translations.idiomatic: Xian believed the ruse and issued a dispatch summoning allied forces for a pincer attack.

sentences.zh: 他將多觀望，憲攻北門，三戰，賊稍卻，與子幹先登逼之。

translations.literal: The other generals mostly held back and watched; Xian attacked the north gate. After three battles the bandits yielded somewhat, and together with his son Gàn he was first to climb the wall and press them.
translations.idiomatic: While the other commanders mostly hung back, Xian assaulted the north gate. After three engagements the bandits began to give ground, and he and his son Gàn were the first to scale the walls and press the attack.

sentences.zh: 賊下木石如雨，軍潰，憲中槍，幹前救，力戰墮崖死。

translations.literal: The bandits rained down timber and stones; the army collapsed. Xian was struck by a spear; Gàn rushed forward to rescue him, fought fiercely, and fell from a cliff to his death.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits rained timber and stones upon them; the army broke. Xian was speared, and Gàn rushed forward to save him, fighting until he fell from a cliff and died.

sentences.zh: 憲創重被執，罵不絕口，賊支解之。

translations.literal: Xian, grievously wounded, was captured. He cursed without cease, and the bandits dismembered him.
translations.idiomatic: Grievously wounded, Xian was taken prisoner. He never stopped cursing, and the bandits dismembered him.

sentences.zh: 事始聞，贈按察使，予祭葬，謚節湣，蔭一子，旌幹門曰孝烈。

translations.literal: When word first reached the throne, he was posthumously made Surveillance Commissioner, granted sacrificial burial, given the posthumous title Jiemin (Steadfast Lamentation), one son was granted hereditary privilege, and Gàn's gate was honored with the inscription "Filial Fierceness."
translations.idiomatic: When news of the affair first reached the throne, Xian was posthumously made surveillance commissioner, granted state burial rites, and given the posthumous title Jiemin (Steadfast Lamentation); one son received hereditary enrollment, and Gàn's family gate was honored with the plaque "Filial Fierceness."

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年，江西巡撫盛應期請與黃宏、馬思聰並旌，詔附禮忠烈祠。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jiajing, Jiangxi Grand Coordinator Sheng Yingqi requested that he be honored together with Huang Hong and Ma Sicong; an edict ordered them enshrined in the Rites Department's Hall of Loyal Martyrs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jiajing, Jiangxi grand coordinator Sheng Yingqi petitioned that Xian be honored together with Huang Hong and Ma Sicong; an edict ordered their names entered in the Ministry of Rites' Hall of Loyal Martyrs.

sentences.zh: 後從給事中李鐸言，命有司歲給其家米二石，帛二匹。

translations.literal: Later, following the memorial of Supervising Secretary Li Duo, the throne ordered the local authorities to grant his household two shi of grain and two bolts of silk each year.
translations.idiomatic: Later, on the recommendation of supervising secretary Li Duo, the throne ordered the local authorities to grant his household two shi of grain and two bolts of silk every year.

sentences.zh: 楊忠，寧夏人。

translations.literal: Yang Zhong, a native of Ningxia.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhong was a native of Ningxia.

sentences.zh: 世官中衛指揮，以功進都指揮僉事，廉介有謀勇。

translations.literal: By hereditary office he was a commander of Zhongwei; for merit he was promoted to Assistant Regional Military Commissioner. He was upright, resolute, and possessed both strategy and courage.
translations.idiomatic: He held hereditary appointment as a commander of Zhongwei and was promoted to assistant regional military commissioner for his deeds. Upright and resolute, he was as clever as he was brave.

sentences.zh: 正德五年，安化王寘鐇反，其黨丁廣將殺巡撫安惟學，忠在側，罵曰：「賊狗敢犯上邪！」

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhengde, the Prince of Anhua, Zhu Zhifan, rebelled. His follower Ding Guang was about to kill Grand Coordinator An Weixue. Zhong was at his side and cursed: "You bandit cur—dare you commit lese majesty?"
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Zhengde, the Prince of Anhua, Zhu Zhifan, rebelled. His follower Ding Guang was about to kill grand coordinator An Weixue. Zhong was at his side and cursed: "You bandit cur—dare you commit lese majesty?"

sentences.zh: 廣怒，殺之，迄死罵益厲。

translations.literal: Guang flew into a rage and killed him; to the end he cursed all the more fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Guang flew into a rage and killed him, yet to his last breath Zhong only cursed the louder.

sentences.zh: 忠同官李睿聞變，馳至寘鐇所。

translations.literal: Zhong's colleague Li Rui, hearing of the uprising, galloped to Zhifan's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong's colleague Li Rui, hearing of the revolt, rode at full speed to Zhifan's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 門閉不得入，大罵，為賊所殺。

translations.literal: The gate was closed and he could not enter; he cursed loudly and was killed by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The gates were barred against him; he cursed loudly and was slain by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 百戶張欽不從逆，走至雷福堡，亦被殺。

translations.literal: Centurion Zhang Qin refused to join the rebellion, fled to Leifu Fort, and was also killed.
translations.idiomatic: Centurion Zhang Qin refused to join the rebellion, fled to Leifu Fort, and was killed there as well.

sentences.zh: 皆贈官予蔭，表忠、睿曰忠烈之門，欽曰忠節之門。

translations.literal: All were posthumously granted office and hereditary privilege; Zhong's and Rui's gates were honored with the inscription "Gate of Loyal Martyrs," and Qin's with "Gate of Loyal Integrity."
translations.idiomatic: All were posthumously granted office and hereditary privilege; the gates of Zhong and Rui were honored with the plaque "Gate of Loyal Martyrs," and Qin's with "Gate of Loyal Integrity."

sentences.zh: 吳景，南陵人。

translations.literal: Wu Jing, a native of Nanling.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Jing was a native of Nanling.

sentences.zh: 弘治九年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the ninth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the ninth year of the Hongzhi reign.

sentences.zh: 正德中，歷官四川僉事，守江津。

translations.literal: During the Zhengde reign he served as Vice Commissioner of Sichuan and defended Jiangjin.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengde reign he served as vice commissioner of Sichuan and defended Jiangjin.

sentences.zh: 重慶人曹弼亡命播州，糾眾寇川南，謀與大盜藍廷瑞合。

translations.literal: Cao Bi of Chongqing, an outlaw in Bozhou, gathered men to raid southern Sichuan and plotted to join forces with the great bandit Lan Tingrui.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Bi of Chongqing, a fugitive in Bozhou, rallied followers to plunder southern Sichuan and planned to join the great bandit chief Lan Tingrui.

sentences.zh: 六年正月逼江津。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year they pressed Jiangjin.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixth year they pressed Jiangjin.

sentences.zh: 御史俞緇遁去，屬景及都指揮龐鳳禦之。

translations.literal: Censor Yu Zi fled; he entrusted Jing and Regional Military Commander Pang Feng to defend against them.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Yu Zi fled, leaving Jing and regional military commander Pang Feng to hold the line.

sentences.zh: 鳳邀景俱走，景不可，率典史張俊迎擊，手殺三賊，矢被面。

translations.literal: Feng invited Jing to flee together; Jing refused, led the county clerk Zhang Jun in a counterattack, killed three bandits with his own hand, and was struck in the face by an arrow.
translations.idiomatic: Feng urged Jing to flee with him, but Jing refused. Leading county clerk Zhang Jun, he met the enemy head-on, killed three bandits with his own hand, and took an arrow in the face.

sentences.zh: 急收兵入保，城已陷，大呼曰：「寧殺我，毋殺士民！」

translations.literal: He hurriedly withdrew the troops into the fort, but the city had already fallen. He cried out: "Better kill me than kill the officials and people!"
translations.idiomatic: He hurriedly withdrew his men to the fort, but the city had already fallen. He cried out: "Better kill me than kill the officials and people!"

sentences.zh: 賊強之跪，不屈，遂被殺，俊亦死。

translations.literal: The bandits forced him to kneel; he would not yield and was then killed; Jun also died.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits forced him to his knees; he would not submit and was killed, and Jun died as well.

sentences.zh: 巡撫林俊上其事，詔贈景副使，賜祭葬，立祠江津，予世蔭。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Lin Jun reported the affair; an edict posthumously made Jing Vice Commissioner, granted sacrificial burial, established a shrine at Jiangjin, and granted hereditary privilege to his descendants.
translations.idiomatic: Grand coordinator Lin Jun reported the affair to the throne. An edict posthumously made Jing a vice commissioner, granted him state burial rites, erected a shrine at Jiangjin, and enrolled his descendants in office.

sentences.zh: 是月，僉事王源行部川北，會藍廷瑞、鄢本恕等掠通、巴至營山，源率典史鄧俊禦之，皆被殺。

translations.literal: That same month, Vice Commissioner Wang Yuan was touring northern Sichuan when Lan Tingrui, Yan Benshu, and others pillaged Tong and Ba as far as Yingshan. Yuan led county clerk Deng Jun to resist; both were killed.
translations.idiomatic: That same month, vice commissioner Wang Yuan was making his rounds in northern Sichuan when Lan Tingrui, Yan Benshu, and others raided through Tongzhou and Bazhou as far as Yingshan. Yuan led county clerk Deng Jun to meet them; both were killed.

sentences.zh: 贈源副使，蔭其子。

translations.literal: Yuan was posthumously made Vice Commissioner, and his son granted hereditary privilege.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was posthumously made a vice commissioner, and his son received hereditary enrollment.

sentences.zh: 源，五臺人，弘治十二年進士。

translations.literal: Yuan was a native of Wutai and a jinshi of the twelfth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was a native of Wutai and had become a jinshi in the twelfth year of the Hongzhi reign.

sentences.zh: 明年正月，賊麻六兒將逼川東。

translations.literal: In the first month of the following year, the bandit Ma Liu'er was about to press eastern Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the following year, the bandit Ma Liu'er was poised to overrun eastern Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 副使馮傑追擊於蒼溪，俘斬頗眾。

translations.literal: Vice Commissioner Feng Jie pursued them at Cangxi and took and beheaded a considerable number.
translations.idiomatic: Vice commissioner Feng Jie pursued them at Cangxi, capturing and killing a great many.

sentences.zh: 日晡，移營鐵山關，賊乘夜沖突，傑死之。

translations.literal: In the late afternoon he moved camp to Tieshan Pass; the bandits rushed them by night, and Jie died.
translations.idiomatic: Toward evening he moved camp to Tieshan Pass; the bandits struck at night, and Jie was killed.

sentences.zh: 贈按察使，賜祭葬，謚恪湣，世蔭百戶。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Surveillance Commissioner, granted sacrificial burial, given the posthumous title Kemin (Reverent Lamentation), and his descendants granted hereditary centurion rank.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made surveillance commissioner, granted state burial rites, given the posthumous title Kemin (Reverent Lamentation), and his line was granted hereditary centurion rank.

sentences.zh: 是時，略陽知縣孫璽、劍州判官羅明、梁山主簿時植亦皆死於賊。

translations.literal: At this time, Sun Xi, magistrate of Lueyang; Luo Ming, assistant prefect of Jianzhou; and Shi Zhi, registrar of Liangshan—all likewise died at the hands of bandits.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Sun Xi, magistrate of Lueyang; Luo Ming, assistant prefect of Jianzhou; and Shi Zhi, registrar of Liangshan—all likewise died fighting the bandits.

sentences.zh: 璽，字廷信，代州人。

translations.literal: Xi, style name Tingxin, a native of Daizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xi, style name Tingxin, was a native of Daizhou.

sentences.zh: 舉於鄉，知扶風縣。

translations.literal: Selected in the provincial examination, he served as magistrate of Fufeng County.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination and served as magistrate of Fufeng County.

sentences.zh: 都御史藍章以略陽漢中要地，舊無城，檄璽往城之。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Lan Zhang, because Lueyang was a strategic point in Hanzhong and had never had a wall, ordered Xi by dispatch to go and build one.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Lan Zhang, knowing that Lueyang was a strategic point in Hanzhong and had never had city walls, ordered Xi by dispatch to go and build them.

sentences.zh: 工未畢，賊至，縣令嚴順欲去，璽拔刀斫坐幾曰：「欲去者視此！」

translations.literal: Before the work was finished, bandits arrived. Magistrate Yan Shun wished to flee; Xi drew his sword and hacked the desk before him, saying: "Whoever wishes to leave—look at this!"
translations.idiomatic: Before the work was finished, bandits arrived. Magistrate Yan Shun wished to flee; Xi drew his sword and hacked the desk before him, saying: "Whoever wishes to leave—look at this!"

sentences.zh: 乃率僚屬堅守，數日城陷，璽被執，大罵不屈，賊臠殺之。

translations.literal: Then he led the staff in a stout defense. After several days the city fell; Xi was captured, cursed loudly and would not yield, and the bandits hacked him to pieces.
translations.idiomatic: He then led his subordinates in a stout defense. When the city fell after several days, Xi was taken captive. He cursed without yielding, and the bandits hacked him to pieces.

sentences.zh: 順逃去，誣璽俱逃，滋於江，以他人屍斂。

translations.literal: Shun fled and falsely claimed that Xi had fled with him; he disposed of the remains in the river and had another man's corpse placed in a coffin.
translations.idiomatic: Shun fled and falsely claimed that Xi had fled with him. He disposed of the remains in the river and had another man's corpse placed in a coffin.

sentences.zh: 璽子啟視，非是，訟於朝。

translations.literal: Xi's son opened the coffin to look; it was not his father, and he appealed to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Xi's son opened the coffin to look and found it was not his father; he brought suit at court.

sentences.zh: 勘得死節狀，贈光祿少卿，賜祭予蔭，抵順罪。

translations.literal: Investigation established the facts of his death in loyalty; he was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, granted sacrificial honors and hereditary privilege, and Shun was punished.
translations.idiomatic: Investigation established that he had died loyal; he was posthumously made vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, granted state burial rites and hereditary enrollment, and Shun was brought to account.

sentences.zh: 明，以吏起家。

translations.literal: Ming began his career as a clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Ming began his career as a clerk.

sentences.zh: 鄢本恕逼其城，與子介拒守。

translations.literal: Yan Benshu pressed his city; he and his son Jie resisted and held it.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan Benshu pressed the city, he and his son Jie held firm in defense.

sentences.zh: 城陷，父子皆罵賊死。

translations.literal: When the city fell, father and son both cursed the bandits and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, father and son both cursed the bandits and died fighting.

sentences.zh: 植，字良材，通許人。

translations.literal: Zhi, style name Liangcai, a native of Tongxu.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zhi, style name Liangcai, was a native of Tongxu.

sentences.zh: 由國子生授官，時攝縣事。

translations.literal: From Imperial Academy student he received appointment; at the time he was acting in county affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed from among the students of the Imperial Academy, he was at the time acting head of county affairs.

sentences.zh: 賊方四等略地，植拒卻之，斬獲數十級。

translations.literal: The bandit Fang Si was overrunning the territory; Zhi repulsed him and beheaded or captured several dozen.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandit Fang Si overran the countryside, Zhi drove him back, killing or capturing several dozen men.

sentences.zh: 逾月復至，相拒數日，城陷，說之降，不屈。

translations.literal: After more than a month they returned; after several days of resistance the city fell. They urged him to surrender; he would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: A month later they returned. After several days of resistance the city fell; they urged him to surrender, but he would not yield.

sentences.zh: 脅取其印，不予，大罵被殺。

translations.literal: They coerced him for the seal; he would not give it and was killed after cursing loudly.
translations.idiomatic: They threatened him for the official seal; he refused and was killed after a torrent of curses.

sentences.zh: 妻賈聞變即自縊，女九歲，赴火死。

translations.literal: His wife Jia, hearing of the disaster, immediately hanged herself; his daughter, nine years old, threw herself into the fire and died.
translations.idiomatic: His wife Jia, hearing what had happened, immediately hanged herself; his nine-year-old daughter threw herself into the fire and died.

sentences.zh: 明、植皆贈恤如制，而表植妻女為貞烈。

translations.literal: Ming and Zhi both received posthumous condolence according to regulation, and Zhi's wife and daughter were honored as chaste martyrs.
translations.idiomatic: Both Ming and Zhi received posthumous honors according to regulation, and plaques were raised honoring Zhi's wife and daughter as chaste martyrs.

sentences.zh: 其時，士民冒死殺賊者，有趙趣、徐敬之、雷應通、袁璋之屬。

translations.literal: At that time among commoners and students who risked death to kill bandits were Zhao Qu, Xu Jingzhi, Lei Yingtong, Yuan Zhang, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, among those scholars and commoners who risked death to kill bandits were Zhao Qu, Xu Jingzhi, Lei Yingtong, Yuan Zhang, and others of that company.

sentences.zh: 趣，梁山諸生。

translations.literal: Qu was a student of Liangshan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Qu was a student of Liangshan.

sentences.zh: 賊攻城，同友人黃甲、李鳳、何璟、蕭銳、徐宣、楊茂寬、趙采誓死拒守。

translations.literal: When bandits besieged the city, together with his friends Huang Jia, Li Feng, He Jing, Xiao Rui, Xu Xuan, Yang Maokuan, and Zhao Cai he swore to die resisting.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits besieged the city, he and his friends Huang Jia, Li Feng, He Jing, Xiao Rui, Xu Xuan, Yang Maokuan, and Zhao Cai swore to die defending it.

sentences.zh: 城陷，皆死。

translations.literal: When the city fell, all died.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, they all died.

sentences.zh: 都物史林俊嘉其義，立祠祀之。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Lin Jun praised their righteousness and established a shrine to sacrifice to them.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-chief Lin Jun commended their righteousness and established a shrine in their honor.

sentences.zh: 敬之，亦梁山人。

translations.literal: Jingzhi was also a native of Liangshan.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingzhi was also a native of Liangshan.

sentences.zh: 眾推為部長，以拒賊陷陣死。

translations.literal: The people chose him as head of the militia company; in resisting the bandits he fell in battle and died.
translations.idiomatic: The people chose him as head of the militia company, and he died in battle fighting the bandits.

sentences.zh: 應通，嘉州人。

translations.literal: Yingtong was a native of Jiazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lei Yingtong was a native of Jiazhou.

sentences.zh: 賊沖百丈關，父子七人倡義死戰。

translations.literal: When bandits stormed Baizhang Pass, father and sons—seven men in all—took the lead in righteous battle unto death.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits stormed Baizhang Pass, a father and his sons—seven men in all—took the lead in righteous battle unto death.

sentences.zh: 被執，俱慷慨就殺。

translations.literal: Captured, all went willingly to execution.
translations.idiomatic: Taken captive, they all went willingly to their deaths.

sentences.zh: 璋，江南人。

translations.literal: Zhang was a native of Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Zhang was a native of Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 素以勇俠聞。

translations.literal: He had long been known for valor and chivalry.
translations.idiomatic: He had long been known for courage and chivalry.

sentences.zh: 巡撫林俊委剿賊所在有功。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Lin Jun entrusted him with suppressing bandits wherever they appeared, and he achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: Grand coordinator Lin Jun charged him with suppressing bandits wherever they appeared, and he served with distinction.

sentences.zh: 後為所執，其子襲挺身救之，連殺七賊，亦被執，俱死。

translations.literal: Later he was captured; his son Xi rushed forward bodily to rescue him, killed seven bandits in succession, was also captured, and both died.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was taken captive; his son Xi rushed forward to rescue him, killing seven bandits in succession before he too was captured, and both died.

sentences.zh: 襲死三日，兩目猶瞠視其父。

translations.literal: Three days after Xi's death, both eyes still stared wide at his father.
translations.idiomatic: Three days after Xi died, his eyes still stared wide toward his father.

sentences.zh: 林俊表其門曰父子忠節。

translations.literal: Lin Jun honored their gate with the inscription "Father and Son, Loyal Integrity."
translations.idiomatic: Lin Jun honored their gate with the plaque "Father and Son, Loyal Integrity."

sentences.zh: 總制彭澤為勒石城隍廟，祀於忠孝祠。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Peng Ze had a stone cut at the City God Temple, and they were sacrificed to in the Hall of Loyalty and Filial Piety.
translations.idiomatic: Grand coordinator Peng Ze had a stone inscription cut at the City God Temple, and they were enshrined in the Hall of Loyalty and Filial Piety.

sentences.zh: 霍恩，字天錫，易州人。

translations.literal: Huo En, style name Tianxi, a native of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huo En, style name Tianxi, was a native of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 弘治十五年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the fifteenth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the fifteenth year of the Hongzhi reign.

sentences.zh: 正德中，歷知上蔡縣。

translations.literal: During the Zhengde reign he served in succession as magistrate of Shangcai County.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengde reign he served as magistrate of Shangcai County.

sentences.zh: 六年，賊四起，中原郡邑多殘破。

translations.literal: In the sixth year bandits rose on every side, and commanderies and counties of the Central Plain were largely devastated.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year bandits rose everywhere, and many commanderies and counties of the Central Plain were laid waste.

sentences.zh: 畿內則棗強知縣段豸、大城知縣張汝舟，河南則恩及典史梁逵，西平知縣王佐、主簿李銓，葉縣知縣唐天恩，永城知縣王鼎，裕州同知郁采、都指揮詹濟、鄉官任賢，固始丞曾基，夏邑丞安宣，息縣主簿刑祥，睢寧主簿金聲、丘紳，西華教諭孔環，山東則萊蕪知縣熊驂，萊州衛指揮僉事蔡顯，南畿則靈譬主簿蔣賢，皆抗節死，而恩、佐、采、環死尤烈。

translations.literal: Within the capital region: Duan Zhi, magistrate of Zaoqiang, and Zhang Ruizhou, magistrate of Dacheng. In Henan: En and county clerk Liang Kui; Wang Zuo, magistrate of Xiping, and registrar Li Quan; Tang Tian'en, magistrate of Ye County; Wang Ding, magistrate of Yongcheng; Yu Cai, vice prefect of Yuzhou, regional military commander Zhan Ji, and local official Ren Xian; Zeng Ji, assistant magistrate of Gushi; An Xuan, assistant magistrate of Xiayi; Xing Xiang, registrar of Xi County; Jin Sheng and Qiu Shen, registrars of Suining; Kong Huan, instructor of Xihua. In Shandong: Xiong Can, magistrate of Laiwu; Cai Xian, assistant regional military commissioner of Laizhou Guard. In the Southern Capital region: Jiang Xian, registrar of Lingbi. All died resisting to the end; En, Zuo, Cai, and Huan died especially fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Within the capital region were Duan Zhi, magistrate of Zaoqiang, and Zhang Ruizhou, magistrate of Dacheng. In Henan were En and county clerk Liang Kui; Wang Zuo, magistrate of Xiping, and registrar Li Quan; Tang Tian'en, magistrate of Ye County; Wang Ding, magistrate of Yongcheng; Yu Cai, vice prefect of Yuzhou, regional military commander Zhan Ji, and local official Ren Xian; Zeng Ji, assistant magistrate of Gushi; An Xuan, assistant magistrate of Xiayi; Xing Xiang, registrar of Xi County; Jin Sheng and Qiu Shen, registrars of Suining; and Kong Huan, instructor of Xihua. In Shandong were Xiong Can, magistrate of Laiwu, and Cai Xian, assistant regional military commissioner of Laizhou Guard. In the Southern Capital region was Jiang Xian, registrar of Lingbi. All died resisting to the end; En, Zuo, Cai, and Huan died especially fiercely.

sentences.zh: 恩與梁逵共守，當賊至時，語妻劉曰：「脫有急，汝若何？」

translations.literal: En and Liang Kui defended together. When bandits arrived, he said to his wife Liu: "If there is an emergency, what will you do?"
translations.idiomatic: En and Liang Kui defended together. When bandits arrived, he said to his wife Liu: "If there is an emergency, what will you do?"

sentences.zh: 劉願同死，乃築臺廨後，約曰：「見我下城，即賊入矣。」

translations.literal: Liu wished to die together with him; they therefore built a platform behind the yamen and agreed: "When you see me descend from the city wall, the bandits have entered."
translations.idiomatic: Liu wished to die with him; they therefore built a platform behind the yamen and agreed: "When you see me descend from the city wall, the bandits have entered."

sentences.zh: 及城陷，恩拔刀下城，劉臺上見之，即縊，未絕，以簪刺心死。

translations.literal: When the city fell, En drew his sword and descended from the wall. Liu saw this from the platform and immediately hanged herself; before life had fully departed, she pierced her heart with a hairpin and died.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, En drew his sword and descended from the wall. Liu saw this from the platform and at once hanged herself; before life had left her, she pierced her heart with a hairpin and died.

sentences.zh: 恩被執，賊脅之跪。

translations.literal: En was captured; the bandits forced him to kneel.
translations.idiomatic: En was taken captive, and the bandits forced him to kneel.

sentences.zh: 罵曰：「吾此膝肯為賊屈乎！」

translations.literal: He cursed: "Would these knees of mine bow to bandits!"
translations.idiomatic: He cursed: "Would these knees of mine bow to bandits!"

sentences.zh: 賊日殺人以懾之，罵益厲。

translations.literal: The bandits daily killed people to intimidate him; he cursed all the more fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits killed people day after day to intimidate him, yet he only cursed the louder.

sentences.zh: 賊以刀抉其口，支解之。

translations.literal: The bandits pried open his mouth with a knife and dismembered him.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits pried his mouth open with a knife and dismembered him.

sentences.zh: 逵自經死。

translations.literal: Kui hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Kui hanged himself to death.

sentences.zh: 豸，字世高，澤洲人。

translations.literal: Zhi, style name Shigao, a native of Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Zhi, style name Shigao, was a native of Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 起家進士。

translations.literal: He began his career as a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He had begun his career as a jinshi.

sentences.zh: 正德中，授兵科都給事中，謫棗強令。

translations.literal: During the Zhengde reign he was appointed supervising secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs and was demoted to magistrate of Zaoqiang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengde reign he was appointed supervising secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs and was later demoted to magistrate of Zaoqiang.

sentences.zh: 賊至，連戰卻之。

translations.literal: When bandits arrived, he fought them repeatedly and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits arrived, he fought them again and again and drove them back.

sentences.zh: 及城陷，中四矢一槍，瞋目大呼，殺賊而死，賊屠其城。

translations.literal: When the city fell, he was struck by four arrows and one spear; with glaring eyes he shouted loudly, killed bandits, and died; the bandits massacred the city.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell he took four arrows and a spear; glaring and shouting, he killed bandits until he died, and the bandits then sacked the city.

sentences.zh: 汝舟官大城時，與主簿李銓迎戰，皆被殺。

translations.literal: When Ruizhou served as magistrate of Dacheng, he and registrar Li Quan met the enemy in battle and both were killed.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as magistrate of Dacheng, Ruizhou and registrar Li Quan met the enemy in battle and both were killed.

sentences.zh: 佐，字汝弼。

translations.literal: Zuo, style name Rubi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zuo, style name Rubi.

sentences.zh: 潞州舉人，授西平令。

translations.literal: A provincial graduate of Luzhou, he was appointed magistrate of Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: A provincial graduate of Luzhou, he was appointed magistrate of Xiping.

sentences.zh: 手殺賊數十人，矢斃其渠帥。

translations.literal: With his own hand he killed several dozen bandits and shot dead their ringleader.
translations.idiomatic: He killed several dozen bandits with his own hand and felled their ringleader with an arrow.

sentences.zh: 賊忿，急攻三日，佐力屈被執，罵不絕口。

translations.literal: The bandits, enraged, pressed the attack for three days; Zuo's strength gave out and he was captured, cursing without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, the bandits pressed the attack for three days. When Zuo's strength gave out he was captured, yet never stopped cursing.

sentences.zh: 賊懸諸竿，殺而支解之。

translations.literal: The bandits hung him on a pole, killed him, and dismembered him.
translations.idiomatic: The bandits hung him from a pole, killed him, and dismembered him.

sentences.zh: 天恩知葉縣，賊至，與父政等七人俱死。

translations.literal: Tian'en served as magistrate of Ye County; when bandits arrived, he and his father Zheng and six others all died together.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Tian'en was magistrate of Ye County; when bandits arrived, he and his father Zheng and six others all died together.

sentences.zh: 鼎知永城，城陷，系印於肘，端坐待賊，不屈死。

translations.literal: Ding served as magistrate of Yongcheng; when the city fell he tied the seal to his elbow, sat upright awaiting the bandits, and died without yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ding was magistrate of Yongcheng; when the city fell he bound the official seal to his elbow, sat upright awaiting the bandits, and died without yielding.

sentences.zh: 采，字亮之，浙江山陰人，進士。

translations.literal: Cai, style name Liangzhi, a native of Shanyin in Zhejiang; a jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Cai, style name Liangzhi, was a native of Shanyin in Zhejiang and a jinshi.

sentences.zh: 由主事謫教諭，遷裕州同知。

translations.literal: From department director he was demoted to instructor, then transferred to vice prefect of Yuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He had served as a department director but was demoted to instructor; he was later appointed vice prefect of Yuzhou.

sentences.zh: 與濟、賢共堅守，斬獲多，城陷被執。

translations.literal: Together with Ji and Xian he firmly defended; many were beheaded and captured; when the city fell he was taken.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Zhan Ji and Ren Xian he held the city resolutely, killing and capturing many of the enemy; when the city fell he was taken captive.

sentences.zh: 采罵不輟，賊碎其輔頰而死。

translations.literal: Cai cursed without cease; the bandits smashed his cheeks and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Cai never stopped cursing them; the bandits smashed his jawbones and killed him.

sentences.zh: 濟亦不屈死。

translations.literal: Ji also died without yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Ji likewise died without yielding.

sentences.zh: 賢嘗為御史，方里居，招邑子三千人拒守，罵賊死，一家死者十三人。

translations.literal: Xian had once been a censor; just then living at home in retirement, he gathered three thousand men of the district to resist and defend; he cursed the bandits and died; thirteen persons of one family died.
translations.idiomatic: Xian had once served as a censor and was then living in retirement at home; he mustered three thousand local men to hold the city, cursed the bandits as he died, and thirteen members of his family perished.

sentences.zh: 基為固始丞，被執，使馭馬不從，被害。

translations.literal: Ji served as assistant magistrate of Gushi; he was captured; they ordered him to drive a horse but he would not obey, and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Ji was assistant magistrate of Gushi; taken captive, he was ordered to serve as a horse groom but refused, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 宣，初授夏邑丞。

translations.literal: Xuan, at first appointed assistant magistrate of Xiayi.
translations.idiomatic: As for Xuan, his first appointment was as assistant magistrate of Xiayi.

sentences.zh: 賊楊虎逼其境，或勸毋往，宣兼程進。

translations.literal: The bandit Yang Hu pressed upon his jurisdiction; some advised him not to go; Xuan pressed on by forced marches.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit Yang Hu was threatening the region; some urged him not to take up the post, but Xuan hurried there by forced marches.

sentences.zh: 抵任七日，賊大至，拒守有功。

translations.literal: Seven days after reaching his post, bandits arrived in force; in resisting and defending he had merit.
translations.idiomatic: Within seven days of taking office, bandits arrived in force; his defense was meritorious.

sentences.zh: 城陷，死之。

translations.literal: The city fell; he died for the cause.
translations.idiomatic: When the city fell, he died defending it.

sentences.zh: 祥已致仕，城陷，罵賊死。

translations.literal: Xiang had already retired from office; when the city fell he cursed the bandits and died.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang had already retired; when the city fell he cursed the bandits and died.

sentences.zh: 聲、紳與義士朱用之迎戰死。

translations.literal: Sheng, Shen, and the righteous man Zhu Yongzhi went forth to battle and died.
translations.idiomatic: Jin Sheng, Qiu Shen, and the local hero Zhu Yongzhi went out to meet the enemy in battle and were killed.

sentences.zh: 環，南宮人。

translations.literal: Huan, a native of Nangong.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Huan was a native of Nangong.

sentences.zh: 由歲貢生授來安知縣，為劉瑾黨所陷，左遷西華教諭。

translations.literal: From annual tribute student he was appointed magistrate of Lu'an; framed by the faction of Liu Jin, he was demoted to instructor of Xihua.
translations.idiomatic: Having entered office as an annual tribute graduate, he was appointed magistrate of Lu'an; framed by Liu Jin's faction, he was demoted to instructor at Xihua.

sentences.zh: 被執，賊曰：「呼我王，即釋汝。」

translations.literal: He was captured; the bandits said: "Call me king, and I will release you."
translations.idiomatic: He was taken captive; the bandits said, "Call me king, and I will release you."

sentences.zh: 厲聲曰：「我恨不得碎汝萬段，肯媚汝求活耶！」

translations.literal: He said in a fierce voice: "I only regret that I cannot cut you into ten thousand pieces—would I fawn on you to save my life!"
translations.idiomatic: He cried out fiercely, "I wish I could cut you into ten thousand pieces—do you think I would fawn on you to save my life!"

sentences.zh: 遂被殺。

translations.literal: He was then killed.
translations.idiomatic: He was then killed.

sentences.zh: 驂為賊所執，與主簿韓塘俱不屈死。

translations.literal: Can was captured by bandits; together with registrar Han Tang he died without yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong Can was captured by bandits; he and registrar Han Tang both died without yielding.

sentences.zh: 顯與三子湛、英、順俱禦盜力戰死。

translations.literal: Xian together with his three sons Zhan, Ying, and Shun all fought bandits with force and died.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xian and his three sons Zhan, Ying, and Shun all fought the bandits with all their strength and were killed.

sentences.zh: 諸人死節事聞，皆贈官賜祭予蔭立祠如制。

translations.literal: When reports of these persons' deaths in upholding their integrity reached the court, all were posthumously promoted, granted sacrificial rites, given yin privileges, and had shrines established according to regulation.
translations.idiomatic: When word of these men's faithful deaths reached the court, each was posthumously promoted, granted sacrificial honors, given hereditary privileges, and had a shrine established according to regulations.

sentences.zh: 恩妻劉贈宜人，建忠節坊旌之。

translations.literal: En's wife Liu was posthumously granted the title Lady; a Memorial Arch of Loyal Integrity was built to honor her.
translations.idiomatic: En's wife Liu was posthumously granted the title Lady, and a Memorial Arch of Loyal Integrity was erected in her honor.

sentences.zh: 天恩、鼎、基、宣、祥諸人，裏貫無考。

translations.literal: As for Tian'en, Ding, Ji, Xuan, Xiang, and the others, their places of origin cannot be verified.
translations.idiomatic: The native places of Tian'en, Ding, Ji, Xuan, Xiang, and the others cannot be established.

sentences.zh: 時有鄭寶，為郁林州同知，署北流縣事。

translations.literal: At that time there was Zheng Bao, serving as vice prefect of Yulin Prefecture and acting in the affairs of Beiliu County.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there was Zheng Bao, vice prefect of Yulin Prefecture, who was acting magistrate of Beiliu County.

sentences.zh: 妖賊李通寶犯北流，寶與子宗珪出戰，皆死。

translations.literal: The demonic bandit Li Tongbao invaded Beiliu; Bao and his son Zonggui went out to battle and both died.
translations.idiomatic: The sorcerer-rebel Li Tongbao attacked Beiliu; Bao and his son Zonggui rode out to fight and both were killed.

sentences.zh: 王振者，為福建黃崎鎮巡檢。

translations.literal: Wang Zhen served as coastal patrol inspector of Huangqi in Fujian.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen served as coastal patrol inspector at Huangqi in Fujian.

sentences.zh: 海寇大至，率三子臣、朝、實迎戰競日。

translations.literal: Sea raiders arrived in force; leading his three sons Chen, Chao, and Shi he met them in battle all day long.
translations.idiomatic: Sea raiders arrived in force; he led his three sons Chen, Chao, and Shi to meet them in battle, fighting all day.

sentences.zh: 伏兵起，振被殺，屍僵立。

translations.literal: Ambush troops rose up; Zhen was killed, and his corpse stood rigid.
translations.idiomatic: An ambush sprang up; Zhen was killed, and his corpse remained standing stiffly upright.

sentences.zh: 三子救之，臣重傷，朝、實皆死。

translations.literal: The three sons rushed to rescue him; Chen was gravely wounded; Chao and Shi both died.
translations.idiomatic: His three sons rushed to his aid; Chen was gravely wounded, and Chao and Shi were both killed.

sentences.zh: 亦予恤有差。

translations.literal: They were also granted relief to varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: They were also granted posthumous honors of varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 孫燧，字德成，余姚人。

translations.literal: Sun Sui, style name Decheng, a native of Yuyao.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sui, style name Decheng, was a native of Yuyao.

sentences.zh: 弘治六年進士。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the sixth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the sixth year of the Hongzhi reign.

sentences.zh: 歷刑部主事，再遷郎中。

translations.literal: He served in succession as department director in the Ministry of Justice, and was twice promoted to bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a department director in the Ministry of Justice and was promoted twice to bureau director.

sentences.zh: 正德中，歷河南右布政使。

translations.literal: During the Zhengde reign he served in succession as Right Administration Commissioner of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengde reign he served as Right Administration Commissioner of Henan.

sentences.zh: 寧王宸濠有逆謀，結中官幸臣，日夜诇中朝事，幸有變。

translations.literal: The Prince of Ning, Chen Hao, harbored treasonous designs; he allied with eunuchs and favored ministers, spying day and night on affairs at court, hoping for upheaval.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Ning, Zhu Chenhao, harbored treasonous designs; he cultivated eunuchs and imperial favorites, spying day and night on affairs at court in hopes of turmoil.

sentences.zh: 又劫持群吏，厚餌之，使為己用。

translations.literal: He also seized hold of officials in groups, lavishly bribing them to serve his own purposes.
translations.idiomatic: He also coerced local officials in groups, lavishing bribes on them to win them to his service.

sentences.zh: 惡巡撫王哲不附己，毒之，得疾，逾年死。

translations.literal: He hated Grand Coordinator Wang Zhe for not siding with him, poisoned him; Wang fell ill and died after more than a year.
translations.idiomatic: Resenting Grand Coordinator Wang Zhe for refusing to join him, he poisoned him; Wang fell ill and died more than a year later.

sentences.zh: 董傑代哲，僅八月亦死。

translations.literal: Dong Jie replaced Zhe; after only eight months he too died.
translations.idiomatic: Dong Jie replaced Wang Zhe, but after only eight months he too was dead.

sentences.zh: 自是，官其地者惴惴，以得去為幸。

translations.literal: From this time onward, officials serving in that region were fearful, counting themselves fortunate to be able to leave.
