translations.idiomatic: From then on, officials assigned to that region lived in constant dread, counting themselves fortunate whenever they could leave.

sentences.zh: 代傑者任漢、俞諫，皆歲餘罷歸。

translations.literal: Those who replaced Jie—Ren Han and Yu Jian—both after a little over a year were dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Those who succeeded Jie—Ren Han and Yu Jian—both served a little over a year before being dismissed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 燧以才節著治聲，廷臣推之代。

translations.literal: Sui was renowned for talent and integrity and noted for his governance; court ministers recommended him as replacement.
translations.idiomatic: Sui was known for both talent and integrity and had won a strong reputation in office; court ministers recommended him for the post.

sentences.zh: 十年十月擢右副都御史，巡撫江西。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the tenth year he was elevated to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and appointed Grand Coordinator of Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the tenth year he was promoted to Right Vice Censor-in-Chief and appointed Grand Coordinator of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 燧聞命嘆曰：「是當死生以之矣。」

translations.literal: When Sui heard the appointment he sighed and said: "For this I must stake my life upon it."
translations.idiomatic: When Sui received the appointment he sighed and said, "For this office I must be prepared to live or die."

sentences.zh: 遣妻子還鄉，獨攜二僮以行。

translations.literal: He sent his wife and children back to their home district and traveled alone with two servant boys.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his wife and children home and set out alone with only two boy attendants.

sentences.zh: 時宸濠逆狀已大露，南昌人洶洶，謂宸濠旦暮得天子。

translations.literal: At that time Chen Hao's rebellious conduct had already been largely exposed; the people of Nanchang were in uproar, saying Chen Hao would become Son of Heaven any day now.
translations.idiomatic: By then Chenhao's treason was largely exposed, and the people of Nanchang were in an uproar, saying he would become emperor at any moment.

sentences.zh: 燧左右悉宸濠耳目，燧防察密，左右不得窺，獨時時為宸濠陳說大義，卒不悛。

translations.literal: Those around Sui were all Chen Hao's eyes and ears; Sui kept close guard so those around him could not pry; only from time to time did he set forth the great principles to Chen Hao, who in the end would not repent.
translations.idiomatic: Those around Sui were all Chenhao's spies; Sui watched them closely so they could not pry into his plans, though from time to time he still tried to persuade Chenhao with righteous argument—to no avail.

sentences.zh: 陰察副使許逵忠勇，可屬大事，與之謀。

translations.literal: He secretly observed that Vice Commissioner Xu Kui was loyal and brave and could be entrusted with great affairs; he consulted with him.
translations.idiomatic: Secretly sizing up Vice Commissioner Xu Kui, he found him loyal and courageous and fit to be entrusted with grave matters, and entered into plans with him.

sentences.zh: 先是，副使胡世寧暴宸濠逆謀，中官幸臣為之地，世寧得罪去。

translations.literal: Earlier, Vice Commissioner Hu Shining had exposed Chen Hao's treasonous plot; eunuchs and favored ministers smoothed things over for him, and Shining was punished and left office.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Vice Commissioner Hu Shining had openly denounced Chenhao's treason; eunuchs and imperial favorites intervened on Chenhao's behalf, and Shining was punished and removed from office.

sentences.zh: 燧念訟言於朝無益，乃托禦他寇預為備。

translations.literal: Sui considered that arguing the case at court would be of no use; he therefore pretended to prepare against other bandits as a pretext for making ready.
translations.idiomatic: Sui judged that pressing the case at court would do no good, so he used the pretext of defending against other enemies to prepare in advance.

sentences.zh: 先城進賢，次城南康、瑞州。

translations.literal: First he fortified Jinxian, then successively Nankang and Ruizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He first fortified Jinxian, then moved on to fortify Nankang and Ruizhou.

sentences.zh: 患建昌縣多盜，割其地，別置安義縣，以漸弭之。

translations.literal: Troubled that Jianchang County had many bandits, he carved out part of its territory and separately established Anyi County to gradually quell them.
translations.idiomatic: Because Jianchang County was plagued by bandits, he carved out part of its territory to establish Anyi County as a way to quell the disorder gradually.

sentences.zh: 而請復饒、撫二州兵備，不得復，則請敕湖東分巡兼理之。

translations.literal: He requested restoration of the military commissioners of Rao and Fu prefectures but was not granted it; he then requested an imperial order that the Eastern Poyang Lake circuit intendant should concurrently administer it.
translations.idiomatic: He petitioned to restore the military commissioners of Rao and Fu, but when that was denied he asked that the Eastern Poyang circuit intendant be authorized to take charge instead.

sentences.zh: 九江當湖沖，最要害，請重兵備道權，兼攝南康、寧州、武寧、瑞昌及湖廣興國、通城，以便控制。

translations.literal: Jiujiang faced the lake assault and was the most critical point; he requested enhanced authority for the military defense circuit, concurrently overseeing Nankang, Ningzhou, Wuning, Ruichang, and in Huguang Xingguo and Tongcheng, so as to facilitate control.
translations.idiomatic: Jiujiang stood on the lake's front line and was the most critical point; he asked that the military defense intendant be given heavier authority, with concurrent jurisdiction over Nankang, Ningzhou, Wuning, Ruichang, and in Huguang Xingguo and Tongcheng, to keep the region under control.

sentences.zh: 廣信橫峰、青山諸窯，地險人悍，則請設通判駐弋陽，兼督旁五縣兵。

translations.literal: At the kilns of Hengfeng and Qingshan in Guangxin, where the terrain was perilous and the people fierce, he requested establishment of a vice prefect stationed at Yiyang to oversee the troops of the five neighboring counties.
translations.idiomatic: At the kilns of Hengfeng and Qingshan in Guangxin, where the terrain was treacherous and the people fierce, he asked that a vice prefect be posted at Yiyang to command the troops of the five neighboring counties.

sentences.zh: 又恐宸濠劫兵器，假討賊，盡出之他所。

translations.literal: He also feared Chen Hao would seize weapons; feigning a campaign against bandits, he had them all moved elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing Chenhao might seize the arsenals, he moved all the weapons elsewhere under the pretense of conducting a bandit-suppression campaign.

sentences.zh: 宸濠間燧圖己，使人賂朝中幸臣去燧，而遣燧棗梨姜芥以示意，燧笑卻之。

translations.literal: Chen Hao heard that Sui was plotting against him and sent men to bribe favored ministers at court to remove Sui; he also sent Sui jujubes, pears, ginger, and mustard to convey his meaning; Sui laughed and refused them.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Sui was working against him, Chenhao sent men to bribe imperial favorites at court to have Sui removed, and sent him jujubes, pears, ginger, and mustard as a hint that he should leave quickly; Sui laughed and refused the gifts.

sentences.zh: 逵勸燧先發後聞，燧曰：「奈何予賊以名，且需之。」

translations.literal: Kui urged Sui to strike first and report afterward; Sui said: "How can I give the bandit a pretext, and besides we must wait."
translations.idiomatic: Kui urged Sui to move first and report afterward; Sui replied, "How can I give the rebels a pretext by name? Besides, we must wait."

sentences.zh: 十三年，江西大水，宸濠素所蓄賊淩十一、吳十三、閔念四等出沒鄱陽湖，燧與逵謀捕之。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Jiangxi suffered great floods; bandits Chen Hao had long kept—Ling Shiyi, Wu Shisan, Min Niansi, and others—roamed Poyang Lake; Sui and Kui plotted to capture them.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year a great flood struck Jiangxi; bandits Chenhao had long harbored—Ling Shiyi, Wu Shisan, Min Niansi, and others—were raiding on Poyang Lake, and Sui and Kui plotted to capture them.

sentences.zh: 三賊遁沙井，燧自江外掩捕，夜大風雨，不克濟。

translations.literal: The three bandits fled to Shajing; Sui from outside the river moved to surround and capture them; at night a great wind and rain arose, and he could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: The three bandits fled to Shajing; Sui tried to trap them from beyond the river, but a violent storm that night prevented him from crossing.

sentences.zh: 三賊走匿宸濠祖墓間，於是密疏白其狀，且言宸濠必反。

translations.literal: The three bandits fled and hid among Chen Hao's ancestral tombs; he therefore sent a secret memorial reporting the situation and stating that Chen Hao would certainly rebel.
translations.idiomatic: The three bandits took refuge near Chenhao's ancestral tombs; Sui then sent a secret memorial describing the situation and declaring that Chenhao would surely rebel.

sentences.zh: 章七上，輒為宸濠遮獄，不得達。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted seven times, but each time Chen Hao intercepted it at the courier station and it could not reach the throne.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted the memorial seven times, but each time Chenhao intercepted it at the post station and it never reached the throne.

sentences.zh: 宸濠恚甚，因宴毒燧，不死。

translations.literal: Chen Hao was greatly enraged; at a banquet he poisoned Sui, but Sui did not die.
translations.idiomatic: Chenhao was furious; he poisoned Sui at a banquet, but Sui survived.

sentences.zh: 燧乞致仕，又不許，憂懼甚。

translations.literal: Sui requested retirement, but this too was not granted; he was greatly anxious and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Sui petitioned to retire, but that too was denied, and his anxiety grew deep.

sentences.zh: 明年，宸濠脅鎮巡官奏其孝行，燧與巡按御史林潮冀藉是少緩其謀，乃共奏於朝。

translations.literal: The next year Chen Hao coerced the provincial military and civil officials to memorialize his filial conduct; Sui and Investigating Censor Lin Chao hoped by this to slow his plot a little, and together submitted a memorial to court.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Chenhao coerced the provincial military and civil officials to memorialize his filial piety; Sui and Investigating Censor Lin Chao hoped this would buy a little time, and jointly submitted a memorial to court.

sentences.zh: 朝議方降旨責燧等，會御史蕭淮盡發宸濠不軌狀，詔重臣宣諭，宸濠聞，遂決計反。

translations.literal: The court was just about to issue an edict rebuking Sui and the others when Censor Xiao Huai fully exposed Chen Hao's rebellious conduct; an edict ordered high ministers to announce the imperial will; when Chen Hao heard this he decided at once to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: The court was on the point of issuing an edict rebuking Sui and the others when Censor Xiao Huai fully exposed Chenhao's treason; the throne ordered high ministers to proclaim the imperial will, and when Chenhao heard this he resolved to rebel at once.

sentences.zh: 六月乙亥，宸濠生日，宴鎮巡三司。

translations.literal: On the yihai day of the sixth month, Chen Hao's birthday, he feasted the provincial military officials and the three commissions.
translations.idiomatic: On the yihai day of the sixth month, Chenhao's birthday, he held a banquet for the provincial military officials and the three commissions.

sentences.zh: 明日，燧及諸大吏入謝，宸濠伏兵左右，大言曰：「孝宗為李廣所誤，抱民間子，我祖宗不血食者十四年。

translations.literal: The next day Sui and the great officials entered to offer thanks; Chen Hao placed ambush troops on either side and declared loudly: "Emperor Xiaozong was misled by Li Guang and raised a commoner's child; my ancestors have gone without blood offerings for fourteen years.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Sui and the senior officials came to offer their thanks; Chenhao had troops hidden on either side and declared loudly, "Emperor Xiaozong was misled by Li Guang and raised a commoner's son as heir; my ancestors have gone without sacrificial offerings for fourteen years.

sentences.zh: 今太后有詔，令我起兵討賊，亦知之乎？」

translations.literal: Now the Empress Dowager has an edict ordering me to raise troops to suppress rebels—do you know this too?"
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager has now issued an edict ordering me to raise troops and suppress rebels—are you aware of this?"

sentences.zh: 眾相顧愕眙，燧直前曰：「安得此言！

translations.literal: The crowd looked at one another in stunned dismay; Sui stepped forward and said: "How can such words be spoken!
translations.idiomatic: The officials stared at one another in shock; Sui stepped forward and cried, "How dare you speak such words!

sentences.zh: 請出詔示我。」

translations.literal: Please produce the edict and show it to me."
translations.idiomatic: Produce the edict and show it to me."

sentences.zh: 宸濠曰：「毋多言，我往南京，汝當扈駕。」

translations.literal: Chen Hao said: "Say no more; I am going to Nanjing—you must escort the imperial procession."
translations.idiomatic: Chenhao said, "Say no more. I am going to Nanjing—you must accompany my retinue."

sentences.zh: 燧大怒曰：「汝速死耳。

translations.literal: Sui said in great anger: "You will die soon.
translations.idiomatic: Sui exploded in rage: "You are hastening to your death.

sentences.zh: 天無二日，吾豈從汝為逆哉！」

translations.literal: Heaven has no two suns—how could I follow you in rebellion!"
translations.idiomatic: Heaven accepts no second sun—do you think I would follow you in treason!"

sentences.zh: 宸濠怒叱燧，燧益怒，急起，不得出。

translations.literal: Chen Hao angrily rebuked Sui; Sui grew angrier still, rose hastily, but could not get out.
translations.idiomatic: Chenhao shouted at Sui in fury; Sui only grew angrier, sprang up at once, but could not get out.

sentences.zh: 宸濠入內殿，易戎服出，麾兵縛燧。

translations.literal: Chen Hao entered the inner hall, changed into military dress, came out, and ordered troops to bind Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Chenhao withdrew to the inner hall, changed into military dress, came back out, and ordered his troops to bind Sui.

sentences.zh: 逵奮曰：「汝曹安得辱天子大臣！」

translations.literal: Kui cried out forcefully: "How dare you insult the Son of Heaven's ministers!"
translations.idiomatic: Kui cried out, "How dare you dishonor the Emperor's ministers!"

sentences.zh: 因以身翼蔽燧，賊並縛逵。

translations.literal: Thereupon with his body he shielded Sui; the rebels bound Kui as well.
translations.idiomatic: He threw himself in front of Sui to shield him, and the rebels bound Kui as well.

sentences.zh: 二人且縛且罵，不絕口，賊擊燧，折左臂，與逵同曳出。

translations.literal: The two men cursed without cease even as they were bound; the rebels struck Sui and broke his left arm; together with Kui he was dragged out.
translations.idiomatic: Even as they were bound, the two men never stopped cursing; the rebels struck Sui and broke his left arm, then dragged him and Kui out together.

sentences.zh: 逵謂燧曰：「我勸公先發者，知有今日故也。」

translations.literal: Kui said to Sui: "The reason I urged you, my lord, to strike first was that I knew this day would come."
translations.idiomatic: Kui said to Sui, "The reason I urged you to move first was that I knew this day would come."

sentences.zh: 燧、逵同遇害惠民門外。

translations.literal: Sui and Kui were both murdered together outside Huimin Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Sui and Kui were both killed together outside Huimin Gate.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史王金、布政使梁宸以下，鹹稽首呼萬歲。

translations.literal: Investigating Censor Wang Jin, Administration Commissioner Liang Chen, and those below—all kowtowed and shouted "Long live!"
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censor Wang Jin, Administration Commissioner Liang Chen, and the officials below all kowtowed and shouted "Long live the Prince!"

sentences.zh: 宸濠遂發兵，偽署三賊為將軍，首遣婁伯徇進賢，為知縣劉源清所斬。

translations.literal: Chen Hao then dispatched troops, falsely appointing the three bandits as generals; he first sent Lou Bo to attack Jinxian, and Lou was beheaded by Magistrate Liu Yuanqing.
translations.idiomatic: Chenhao then raised his army, falsely appointing the three bandits as generals; he first sent Lou Bo to strike at Jinxian, and Lou was beheaded by Magistrate Liu Yuanqing.

sentences.zh: 招窯賊，賊畏守吏，不敢發。

translations.literal: He recruited kiln bandits, but the bandits feared the defending officials and dared not rise.
translations.idiomatic: He tried to recruit the kiln bandits, but they feared the local defenders and dared not rebel.

sentences.zh: 大索兵器於城中，不得，賊多持白梃。

translations.literal: He searched the city extensively for weapons but found none; the rebels mostly carried plain clubs.
translations.idiomatic: A thorough search of the city turned up no weapons; most of the rebels ended up wielding plain wooden clubs.

sentences.zh: 伍文定起義兵，設兩人木主於文天祥祠，率吏民哭之。

translations.literal: Wu Wending raised a righteous army, set up wooden spirit tablets for the two men in the Wen Tianxiang shrine, and led officials and people to weep for them.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Wending raised a loyalist force, placed wooden spirit tablets for the two men in the shrine of Wen Tianxiang, and led officials and commoners to mourn them.

sentences.zh: 南贛巡撫王守仁與共平賊。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator of Southern Gan Wang Shouren together with him pacified the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shouren, Grand Coordinator of Southern Gan, joined him in suppressing the rebels.

sentences.zh: 諸逋賊走安義，皆見獲，無脫者。

translations.literal: The various fleeing bandits ran to Anyi; all were captured; none escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The fleeing bandits retreated to Anyi, where they were all captured—not one escaped.

sentences.zh: 人於是益思燧功。

translations.literal: People therefore thought all the more of Sui's achievements.
translations.idiomatic: People then appreciated Sui's foresight all the more.

sentences.zh: 燧生有異質，兩目爍爍，夜有光。

translations.literal: From birth Sui had an extraordinary nature; his two eyes gleamed, and at night there was light.
translations.idiomatic: From birth Sui had an extraordinary nature; his eyes shone brightly, and at night they gave off light.

sentences.zh: 死之日，天忽陰慘，烈風驟起凡數日，城中民大恐。

translations.literal: On the day of his death Heaven suddenly turned gloomy and dismal; fierce winds suddenly arose for several days; the people of the city were greatly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he died the sky suddenly turned dark and ominous, and fierce winds blew for days; the townspeople were terrified.

sentences.zh: 走收兩人屍，屍未變，黑雲蔽之，蠅蚋無近者。

translations.literal: People ran to recover the two corpses; the corpses had not decayed; black clouds covered them, and flies and gnats did not approach.
translations.idiomatic: People rushed to recover the two bodies; the corpses had not yet decayed, black clouds shrouded them, and flies and gnats would not come near.

sentences.zh: 明年，守臣上其事於朝，未報。

translations.literal: The next year defending officials reported the matter to court, but received no response.
translations.idiomatic: The following year local officials reported these events to court, but no reply came.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，贈禮部尚書，謚忠烈，與逵並祀南昌，賜祠名旌忠，各蔭一子。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong ascended the throne, Sui was posthumously granted Minister of Rites, given the posthumous name Zhonglie (Loyal and Fierce), and jointly enshrined with Kui in Nanchang; the shrine was granted the name Jingzhong (Exalting Loyalty), and each man's son was granted yin privilege.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiajing Emperor came to the throne, Sui was posthumously made Minister of Rites and given the posthumous name Loyal and Fierce; he and Kui were jointly enshrined in Nanchang in a temple named Exalting Loyalty, and each man's son received hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 燧子堪聞父訃，率兩弟墀、升赴之，會宸濠已擒，扶柩歸。

translations.literal: Sui's son Kan, hearing of his father's death, led his two younger brothers Chi and Sheng to go there; Chen Hao had already been captured; they escorted the coffin home.
translations.idiomatic: Sui's son Kan, on hearing of his father's death, set out with his two younger brothers Chi and Sheng; Chenhao had already been captured, and they escorted the coffin home.

sentences.zh: 兄弟廬墓蔬食三年，有芝一莖九葩者數本產墓上。

translations.literal: The brothers lived by the tomb in a hut and ate vegetables for three years; several stalks of lingzhi with one stem and nine flowers sprang up on the tomb.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers lived in a hut by the tomb and ate plain food for three years; several lingzhi mushrooms with nine petals on a single stalk appeared on the grave.

sentences.zh: 服除，以父死難，更墨衰三年，世稱三孝子。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, because their father had died in calamity they wore black mourning for three more years; the age called them the Three Filial Sons.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning period ended, they donned black mourning for another three years because their father had died in service; the age hailed them as the Three Filial Sons.

sentences.zh: 堪，字誌健。

translations.literal: Kan, style name Zhijian.
translations.idiomatic: Kan, style name Zhijian.

sentences.zh: 為諸生，能文，善騎射。

translations.literal: He was a licentiate, skilled in writing, adept at horsemanship and archery.
translations.idiomatic: He was a student of the imperial academy, skilled in letters and adept at horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 既蔭錦衣，中武會試第一，擢署指揮同知。

translations.literal: Having received yin privilege in the Embroidered Uniform Guard, he placed first in the military metropolitan examination and was promoted to acting Vice Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Having entered the Embroidered Uniform Guard through inherited privilege, he ranked first in the military metropolitan examination and was appointed acting Vice Commander.

sentences.zh: 善用強弩，教弩卒數千人以備邊。

translations.literal: He was skilled in using powerful crossbows and trained several thousand crossbow soldiers to guard the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled with heavy crossbows, he trained several thousand crossbowmen to defend the frontier.

sentences.zh: 歷都督僉事。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Assistant Commissioner-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He eventually rose to Assistant Commissioner-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 事母楊至孝，母年九十余，歿京師。

translations.literal: He served his mother Yang with utmost filial piety; she was over ninety years old and died in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He served his mother Yang with the utmost filial devotion; she was more than ninety when she died in the capital.

sentences.zh: 堪年亦七十，護喪歸，在道，以毀卒。

translations.literal: Kan was also seventy; escorting the coffin home, on the road he died from grief.
translations.idiomatic: Kan himself was seventy; while escorting her coffin home, he died on the road from the strain of mourning.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史趙炳然上堪孝行，得旌。

translations.literal: Investigating Censor Zhao Bingran reported Kan's filial conduct; he received official commendation.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censor Zhao Bingran memorialized Kan's filial conduct, and he was officially commended.

sentences.zh: 堪子鈺，亦舉武會試，官都督同知。

translations.literal: Kan's son Yu also passed the military metropolitan examination and served as Vice Commissioner-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Kan's son Yu also passed the military metropolitan examination and rose to Vice Commissioner-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 鈺子如津，都督僉事。

translations.literal: Yu's son Rujin was Assistant Commissioner-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's son Rujin served as Assistant Commissioner-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 墀，字仲泉，以選貢生歷官尚寶卿。

translations.literal: Chi, style name Zhongquan, rose through office from selected tribute student to Director of the Imperial Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: Chi, style name Zhongquan, entered service as a selected tribute student and eventually served as Director of the Imperial Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 升，官尚書。

translations.literal: Sheng served as Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng rose to ministerial rank.

sentences.zh: 墀孫如遊，大學士。

translations.literal: Chi's grandson Ruyou was a Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Chi's grandson Ruyou became a Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 如遊孫嘉績，僉事。

translations.literal: Ruyou's grandson Jiaji was a Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyou's grandson Jiaji served as a vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 升子，鑨、鑛皆尚書，鋌侍郎，錝太仆卿。

translations.literal: Sheng's sons: Long and Kuang were both ministers; Ting was Vice Minister; Cong was Director of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng's sons Long and Kuang both reached ministerial rank; Ting became a vice minister and Cong Director of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 鑨子，如法主事，如洵參政。

translations.literal: Long's sons: Rufa was a Department Director; Ruxun was Administration Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Long's sons Rufa and Ruxun served as a department director and an administration commissioner, respectively.

sentences.zh: 並以文章行誼世其家。

translations.literal: All passed down literary talent and moral conduct through their family.
translations.idiomatic: They all handed down literary accomplishment and upright conduct through the generations.

sentences.zh: 升、鑨、鑛、如遊、如法、嘉績，事皆別見。

translations.literal: Sheng, Long, Kuang, Ruyou, Rufa, and Jiaji—their affairs are all treated separately elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: The careers of Sheng, Long, Kuang, Ruyou, Rufa, and Jiaji are all recounted in separate entries.

sentences.zh: 許逵，字汝登，固始人。

translations.literal: Xu Kui, style name Rudeng, a native of Gushi.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Kui, style name Rudeng, was a native of Gushi.

sentences.zh: 正德三年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi of the third year of Zhengde.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the third year of the Zhengde reign.

sentences.zh: 長身巨口，猿臂燕頷，沈靜有謀略。

translations.literal: Tall of stature, large of mouth, with ape-like arms and a swallow's jaw, calm and possessed of strategy.
translations.idiomatic: He was tall and broad-mouthed, with long arms and a strong jaw; quiet by nature, he was thoughtful and resourceful.

sentences.zh: 授樂陵知縣。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Leling.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Leling.

sentences.zh: 六年春，流賊劉七等屠城邑，殺長吏。

translations.literal: In the spring of the sixth year, roving bandits Liu Qi and others slaughtered cities and towns and killed chief officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the sixth year, roving bandits under Liu Qi and others ravaged towns, killing senior officials.

sentences.zh: 諸州縣率閉城守，或棄城遁，或遺之芻，粟弓馬乞賊毋攻。

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties mostly closed their walls and defended, or abandoned their cities and fled, or sent them fodder, grain, bows, and horses begging the bandits not to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures and counties mostly shut their gates and held firm, fled altogether, or sent fodder, grain, bows, and horses begging the bandits to spare them.

sentences.zh: 逵之官，慨然為戰守計。

translations.literal: When Kui took office, he resolutely made plans for fighting and defense.
translations.idiomatic: When Kui arrived to take office, he resolutely set about plans for fighting and defense.

sentences.zh: 縣初無城，督民版築，不逾月，城成。

translations.literal: The county at first had no wall; he superintended the people in rammed-earth construction, and in less than a month the wall was complete.
translations.idiomatic: The county had no wall at first; he organized the people to build one with rammed earth, and within a month it was finished.

sentences.zh: 令民屋外築墻，墻高過檐，啟圭竇，才容人。

translations.literal: He ordered the people to build walls outside their houses, higher than the eaves, with narrow doors just wide enough for one person.
translations.idiomatic: He had people build walls outside their homes, taller than the roofline, with narrow gateways barely wide enough for a single person.

sentences.zh: 家選一壯者執刃伺竇內，余皆入隊伍，日視旗為號，違者軍法從事。

translations.literal: Each household chose one strong man to hold a blade and wait inside the gate; the rest entered military formations; each day they took the flag as signal; violators were dealt with by military law.
translations.idiomatic: Each household detailed one able man to wait inside the gate with a blade at the ready, while the rest joined militia units that rallied to the flag each day; anyone who disobeyed was punished under military law.

sentences.zh: 又募死士伏巷中，洞開城門。

translations.literal: He also recruited daredevils to lie in ambush in the lanes and threw the city gates wide open.
translations.idiomatic: He also recruited daredevils to lie in wait in the alleys while leaving the city gates standing open.

sentences.zh: 賊果至，旗舉伏發，竇中人皆出，賊大驚竄，斬獲無遺。

translations.literal: When the bandits indeed came, the flag was raised and the ambush struck; the men in the gateways all rushed out; the bandits fled in great alarm; none escaped capture or death.
translations.idiomatic: When the bandits came as expected, the signal flag went up, the ambush sprang, and the men at the gates poured out; the bandits fled in panic, and every one was killed or captured.

sentences.zh: 後數犯，數卻之，遂相戒不敢近。

translations.literal: Later they raided several times and were repeatedly repulsed; eventually they warned one another not to approach.
translations.idiomatic: They attacked several more times and were driven back each time, until they warned one another not to come near.

sentences.zh: 事聞，進秩二等。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, he was promoted two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: When word reached court, he was promoted two ranks.

sentences.zh: 時知縣能抗賊者，益都則牛鸞，郯城則唐龍，汶上則左經，浚則陳滯，亦所當賊少。

translations.literal: At the time among magistrates who could resist bandits: in Yidu was Niu Luan, in Tancheng was Tang Long, in Wenshang was Zuo Jing, in Jun was Chen Zhi—they too met bandits in lesser numbers.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the magistrates who could stand up to bandits included Niu Luan of Yidu, Tang Long of Tancheng, Zuo Jing of Wenshang, and Chen Zhi of Jun—though they faced smaller bands.

sentences.zh: 而逵屢禦大賊有功，遂與鸞俱超擢兵備僉事。

translations.literal: But Kui repeatedly repulsed major bandits with merit, and so he and Luan were both promoted by special selection to Assistant Regional Military Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Kui, however, repeatedly drove off major bandit forces with distinction, and he and Luan were both specially promoted to assistant regional military inspector.

sentences.zh: 逵駐武定州，州城圮濠平，不能限牛馬。

translations.literal: Kui was stationed at Wuding Prefecture; the prefectural walls had collapsed and the moat was level, unable to restrain cattle and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Kui was posted to Wuding Prefecture, where the city walls had fallen in and the moat was filled level, so that nothing kept out cattle or horses.

sentences.zh: 逵築城鑿池，設樓櫓，置巡卒。

translations.literal: Kui built walls, dug moats, set up watchtowers and battlements, and posted patrol soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Kui rebuilt the walls, dug out the moat, erected watchtowers, and posted patrols.

sentences.zh: 明年五月，賊楊寡婦以千騎犯濰縣，指揮喬剛禦之，賊少卻。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the next year the bandit Yang the Widow led a thousand horsemen to raid Wei County; Commander Qiao Gang resisted them and the bandits retreated slightly.
translations.idiomatic: The following May the bandit leader Yang the Widow struck Wei County with a thousand horsemen; Commander Qiao Gang met them and forced a partial retreat.

sentences.zh: 逵追敗之高苑，令指揮張勛邀之滄州，先後俘斬二百七十余余人。

translations.literal: Kui pursued and defeated them at Gaoyuan, ordered Commander Zhang Xun to intercept them at Cangzhou, and in succession captured and beheaded more than two hundred seventy men.
translations.idiomatic: Kui pursued and routed them at Gaoyuan and sent Commander Zhang Xun to cut them off at Cangzhou; in all more than two hundred seventy bandits were captured or killed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，賊別部掠德平，逵盡殲之，鹹名大著。

translations.literal: Before long a separate bandit band plundered Deping; Kui annihilated them entirely, and his name for might grew great.
translations.idiomatic: Before long another bandit band raided Deping; Kui wiped them out entirely, and his fame as a fighter spread far.

sentences.zh: 十二年遷江西副使。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was transferred to Jiangxi as Vice Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was transferred to Jiangxi as vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時宸濠黨暴橫，逵以法痛繩之。

translations.literal: At the time Chen Hao's faction was violently overbearing; Kui punished them severely by law.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Chenhao's faction ran rampant; Kui punished them harshly under the law.

sentences.zh: 嘗言於孫燧曰：「寧王敢為暴者，恃權臣也。

translations.literal: He once said to Sun Sui: The Prince of Ning dares to act violently because he relies on powerful court officials.
translations.idiomatic: He once said to Sun Sui, "The Prince of Ning dares to act violently because he relies on powerful court officials.

sentences.zh: 權臣左右之者，貪重賄也。

translations.literal: Those at court who support such officials do so because they covet heavy bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Those at court who champion such officials do so because they covet heavy bribes.

sentences.zh: 重賄由於盜藪，今惟翦盜則賄息，賄息則黨孤。」

translations.literal: Heavy bribes come from dens of bandits; now if we cut down banditry alone, bribes will cease; when bribes cease, the faction will stand isolated."
translations.idiomatic: Heavy bribes flow from bandit dens; if we cut down banditry, bribes will dry up, and once bribes dry up, the faction will stand alone."

sentences.zh: 燧深然之，每事輒與密議。

translations.literal: Sun Sui agreed deeply and on every matter would confer with him in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Sui strongly agreed and consulted with him in secret on every matter.

sentences.zh: 及宸濠縛燧，逵爭之。

translations.literal: When Chen Hao bound Sun Sui, Kui contended with him.
translations.idiomatic: When Chenhao seized Sun Sui, Kui protested.

sentences.zh: 宸濠素忌逵，問許副使何言，逵曰：「副使惟赤心耳。」

translations.literal: Chen Hao had long resented Kui; he asked what Vice Commissioner Xu had said, and Kui replied: The vice commissioner has only a loyal heart."
translations.idiomatic: Chenhao had long resented Kui and asked what Vice Commissioner Xu had said; Kui replied, "The vice commissioner has nothing but a loyal heart."

sentences.zh: 宸濠怒曰：「我不能殺汝邪？」

translations.literal: Chen Hao angrily said: Can I not kill you?"
translations.idiomatic: Chenhao flew into a rage and said, "Can I not kill you?"

sentences.zh: 逵罵曰：「汝能殺我，天子能殺汝。

translations.literal: Kui cursed and said: You can kill me, but the Son of Heaven can kill you.
translations.idiomatic: Kui cursed back, "You can kill me, but the Son of Heaven can kill you.

sentences.zh: 汝反賊，萬段磔汝，汝悔何及！」

translations.literal: You rebel traitor! I would tear you to pieces in ten thousand strips—what regret would that leave you!"
translations.idiomatic: You rebel traitor! I would have you torn to pieces—what regret could you then feel!"

sentences.zh: 宸濠大怒，並縛之，曳出斫其頸，屹不動。

translations.literal: Chen Hao was greatly enraged, had him bound as well, dragged him out and hacked at his neck; he stood unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: Chenhao was furious; he had Kui bound as well, dragged him out, and hacked at his neck, but Kui stood unmoved.

sentences.zh: 賊眾共推抑令跪，卒不能，遂死，年三十六。

translations.literal: The rebel host together pressed him down to make him kneel but in the end could not; he then died, aged thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels together tried to force him to his knees but failed; in the end he died, aged thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 初，逵以文天祥集貽其友給事中張漢卿而無書。

translations.literal: Earlier, Kui gave the collected works of Wen Tianxiang to his friend, Supervising Secretary Zhang Hanqing, but without a letter.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Kui had sent the collected works of Wen Tianxiang to his friend, Supervising Secretary Zhang Hanqing, without enclosing a letter.

sentences.zh: 漢卿語人曰：「寧邸必反，汝登其為文山乎？」

translations.literal: Hanqing told others: The Ning residence is certain to rebel—will Rudeng be its Wen Tianxiang?"
translations.idiomatic: Hanqing told others, "The Prince of Ning is sure to rebel—will Rudeng prove to be his Wen Tianxiang?"

sentences.zh: 逵父家居，聞江西有變，殺都御史及副使，即為位，易服哭。

translations.literal: When Kui's father was at home and heard that trouble had broken out in Jiangxi and that the censor-in-chief and vice commissioner had been killed, he immediately set up a mourning tablet, changed his clothes, and wept.
translations.idiomatic: While Kui's father was at home, he heard that rebellion had broken out in Jiangxi and that the censor-in-chief and a vice commissioner had been killed; he immediately set up a spirit tablet, changed his clothes, and wept.

sentences.zh: 人怪問故。

translations.literal: People wondered and asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: People were astonished and asked why.

sentences.zh: 父曰：「副使，必吾兒也。」

translations.literal: His father said: The vice commissioner must be my son."
translations.idiomatic: His father said, "The vice commissioner must be my son."

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，贈左副都御史，謚忠節，蔭一子。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong ascended the throne, Kui was posthumously granted Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, given the posthumous name Zhongjie (Loyal Integrity), and one son received yin privilege.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiajing Emperor came to the throne, Kui was posthumously made Left Vice Censor-in-Chief, given the posthumous name Loyal Integrity, and one son received hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 又錄山東平賊功，復蔭一子。

translations.literal: His service in suppressing bandits in Shandong was also recorded, and one more son received yin privilege.
translations.idiomatic: His record in pacifying bandits in Shandong was also honored, and another son received hereditary privilege.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖元年詔逵死事尤烈，改贈逵禮部尚書，進蔭指揮僉事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jiajing an edict declared that Kui's death in service was especially fierce; he was posthumously re-granted Minister of Rites, and yin privilege was advanced to Assistant Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jiajing an edict declared Kui's death in service especially valiant; he was posthumously reappointed Minister of Rites, and hereditary privilege was raised to assistant commander.

sentences.zh: 長子玚，好學有器識。

translations.literal: His eldest son Yang was fond of learning and possessed capacity and judgment.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Yang was studious and had breadth of mind.

sentences.zh: 既葬父，日夜號泣，六年而後就蔭。

translations.literal: After burying his father, he wept and wailed day and night; only after six years did he accept yin privilege.
translations.idiomatic: After burying his father, he wept day and night; only after six years did he accept hereditary office.

sentences.zh: 人或趣之，玚曰：「吾父死，玚乃因得官。」

translations.literal: Some urged him on; Yang said: My father died, and only then did Yang obtain office through this."
translations.idiomatic: When others urged him, Yang said, "My father died, and only then did Yang obtain office through it."

sentences.zh: 痛哭不能仰視。

translations.literal: He wept bitterly and could not lift his face.
translations.idiomatic: He wept so bitterly he could not raise his face.

sentences.zh: 玚子䢿，事親孝。

translations.literal: Yang's son Anqiu served his parents with filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Yang's son Anqiu was filial toward his parents.

sentences.zh: 隆慶中舉於鄉，數試禮部不第。

translations.literal: In the Longqing reign he passed the provincial examination; he tried the Ministry of Rites examination several times without placing.
translations.idiomatic: During the Longqing reign he passed the provincial examination but failed the metropolitan examinations several times.

sentences.zh: 有試官與玚婚姻，慕䢿才，欲收羅之。

translations.literal: An examiner was related by marriage to Yang, admired Anqiu's talent, and wished to recruit him.
translations.idiomatic: One examiner was related to Yang by marriage, admired Anqiu's talent, and wished to favor him.

sentences.zh: 䢿曰：「若此，何以見先忠節地下？」

translations.literal: Anqiu said: If I did this, how could I face my late ancestor of Loyal Integrity below?"
translations.idiomatic: Anqiu said, "If I accepted that, how could I face my late ancestor of Loyal Integrity in the grave?"

sentences.zh: 許氏子孫不如孫氏貴顯，亦能傳其家。

translations.literal: The Xu descendants did not attain the rank and prominence of the Sun clan, yet they too could carry on their house.
translations.idiomatic: The Xu descendants never rose as high as the Sun clan, yet they too preserved their family tradition.

sentences.zh: 黃宏，字德裕，鄞人。

translations.literal: Huang Hong, style name Deyu, a native of Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Hong, style name Deyu, was a native of Yin.

sentences.zh: 弘治十五年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi of the fifteenth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the fifteenth year of the Hongzhi reign.

sentences.zh: 知萬安縣。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Wan'an.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Wan'an County.

sentences.zh: 民好訟，訟輒禱於神，宏毀其祠曰：「令在，何禱也。」

translations.literal: The people were fond of litigation; litigants always prayed to the spirits; Hong destroyed their shrine, saying: The magistrate is here—why pray?"
translations.idiomatic: The people were litigious and always prayed to local spirits when they went to court; Hong tore down the shrine and said, "The magistrate is here—why pray?"

sentences.zh: 訟者至，輒片言折之。

translations.literal: When litigants came, he would settle matters in a few words.
translations.idiomatic: When litigants arrived, he settled their disputes in a few words.

sentences.zh: 累遷江西左參議，按湖西、嶺北二道。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Left Administration Commissioner of Jiangxi, inspecting the Huxi and Lingbei circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Left Administration Commissioner of Jiangxi and inspected the Huxi and Lingbei circuits.

sentences.zh: 王守仁討橫水、桶岡賊，宏主餉有功。

translations.literal: Wang Shouren campaigned against the Hengshui and Tonggang bandits; Hong managed supplies with merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shouren campaigned against the bandits of Hengshui and Tonggang, Hong directed provisions and distinguished himself.

sentences.zh: 賊閔念四既降，復恃宸濠勢，剽九江上下。

translations.literal: The bandit Min Niansi having surrendered, again relied on Chen Hao's power and raided up and down the Jiujiang region.
translations.idiomatic: The bandit Min Niansi, though he had surrendered, again relied on Chenhao's power and plundered up and down the Jiujiang region.

sentences.zh: 宏發兵捕之，走匿宸濠祖墓中，盡得其輜重以歸。

translations.literal: Hong sent troops to capture him; Min fled and hid in Chen Hao's ancestral tombs; Hong recovered all his baggage train and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Hong sent troops after him; Min fled and hid among Chenhao's ancestral tombs, and Hong recovered all his baggage and returned.

sentences.zh: 宸濠逆節益露，士大夫以為憂，宏正色曰：「國家不幸有此，我輩守士，死而已。」

translations.literal: As Chen Hao's treasonous conduct became increasingly plain, scholars and officials were troubled; Hong said with stern countenance: The state is unlucky to have this—we who hold our posts need only die."
translations.idiomatic: As Chenhao's treason became plain, officials grew anxious; Hong said sternly, "The state is unlucky to face this—we who hold our posts need only die."

sentences.zh: 有持大義不從宸濠黨者，宏每陰左右之。

translations.literal: Those who upheld the greater principle and would not follow Chen Hao's faction, Hong would secretly aid whenever he could.
translations.idiomatic: For those who upheld righteousness and refused to follow Chenhao's faction, Hong would quietly lend support whenever he could.

sentences.zh: 宸濠反，宏被執，憤怒，以手梏向柱擊項，是夕卒，賊義而棺斂之。

translations.literal: When Chen Hao rebelled, Hong was seized; enraged, he struck his neck against a pillar with his manacled hands and died that night; the rebels, respecting him, coffined him for burial.
translations.idiomatic: When Chenhao rebelled, Hong was seized; in rage he smashed his neck against a pillar with his manacled hands and died that night; the rebels, moved by his integrity, coffined him for burial.

sentences.zh: 子紹文奔赴，求得其棺，以偽命治斂，非父誌，亟易之，扶歸。

translations.literal: His son Shaowen rushed to the scene, found his coffin, and since the rebels had buried him by false command contrary to his father's wishes, quickly replaced the rites and escorted the body home.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shaowen hurried to the scene, recovered the coffin, found the rebels had buried his father by false command against his wishes, promptly replaced the rites, and escorted the body home.

sentences.zh: 時主事馬思聰亦抗節死。

translations.literal: At the time Department Director Ma Sicong also died resisting to uphold integrity.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Department Director Ma Sicong also died upholding his integrity.

sentences.zh: 思聰，字懋聞，莆田人。

translations.literal: Sicong, style name Maowen, a native of Putian.
translations.idiomatic: Sicong, style name Maowen, was a native of Putian.

sentences.zh: 弘治末舉進士，為象山知縣，復二十六渠，溉田萬頃。

translations.literal: At the end of Hongzhi he passed the metropolitan examination; as magistrate of Xiangshan he restored twenty-six canals and irrigated ten thousand qing of fields.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Hongzhi reign he passed the metropolitan examination; as magistrate of Xiangshan he restored twenty-six canals and irrigated ten thousand qing of farmland.

sentences.zh: 累遷南京戶部主事，督糧江西，駐安仁。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Department Director in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue, supervising grain in Jiangxi, stationed at Anren.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to department director in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue, took charge of grain supplies in Jiangxi, and was stationed at Anren.

sentences.zh: 值宸濠反，被執系獄，不屈，絕食六日死。

translations.literal: When Chen Hao rebelled, he was seized and imprisoned; he would not submit and died after six days without food.
translations.idiomatic: When Chenhao rebelled, he was seized and imprisoned; refusing to yield, he starved himself to death after six days.

sentences.zh: 世宗立，贈宏太常少卿，思聰光祿少卿，並配享旌忠祠。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong ascended the throne, Hong was posthumously granted Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Sicong Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; both were jointly enshrined in the Jingzhong Shrine.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jiajing Emperor came to the throne, Hong was posthumously made Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Sicong Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments; both were enshrined in the Exalting Loyalty shrine.

sentences.zh: 時有謂宏、思聰死節非真者。

translations.literal: At the time some said Hong and Sicong's death in upholding integrity was not genuine.
translations.idiomatic: At the time some claimed Hong and Sicong had not truly died for principle.

sentences.zh: 給事中毛玉勘江西逆黨，復請表章宏、思聰及承奉周儀，而宏子紹武訴於朝。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary Mao Yu investigated the Jiangxi rebel faction and again requested official commendation for Hong, Sicong, and Palace Attendant Zhou Yi; Hong's son Shaowu appealed at court.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary Mao Yu investigated the Jiangxi rebels and again petitioned to honor Hong, Sicong, and Palace Attendant Zhou Yi; Hong's son Shaowu lodged an appeal at court.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史穆相列上二人死節狀甚悉，遂無異議。

translations.literal: Investigating Censor Mu Xiang submitted in detail the circumstances of the two men's deaths in upholding integrity; thereupon no further dispute arose.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating Censor Mu Xiang submitted a detailed account of both men's martyrdom, and the doubt was laid to rest.

sentences.zh: 宋以方，字義卿，靖州人。

translations.literal: Song Yifang, style name Yiqing, a native of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Song Yifang, style name Yiqing, was a native of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 弘治十八年進士。

translations.literal: Jinshi of the eighteenth year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the eighteenth year of the Hongzhi reign.

sentences.zh: 歷戶部郎中。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Department Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the Ministry of Revenue, eventually as a department director.

sentences.zh: 正德十年遷瑞州知府。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhengde he was transferred to Prefect of Ruizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of the Zhengde reign he was appointed prefect of Ruizhou.

sentences.zh: 時華林大盜甫平，瘡痍未復，以方悉心撫字，吏民愛之。

translations.literal: At the time the Hualin Great Bandits had just been pacified and wounds had not yet healed; Yifang devoted himself to governing and cherishing the people; officials and commoners loved him.
translations.idiomatic: The Hualin bandits had just been suppressed and the region lay in ruins; Yifang devoted himself to rebuilding the land, and officials and people alike loved him.

sentences.zh: 宸濠逆謀萌，而瑞故無城郭，以方築城繕守具，募兵三千，日夕訓練。

translations.literal: As Chen Hao's treasonous plot arose, Ruizhou had never had walls; Yifang built walls, repaired defense equipment, recruited three thousand soldiers, and trained them day and night.
translations.idiomatic: As Chenhao's treason took shape, Ruizhou still had no walls; Yifang built fortifications, gathered arms, recruited three thousand troops, and drilled them day and night.

sentences.zh: 宸濠深忌之，有征索又不應，遂迫鎮守劾系南昌獄。

translations.literal: Chen Hao deeply resented him; when there were demands he again would not comply; he then forced the garrison commander to impeach and imprison him in Nanchang jail.
translations.idiomatic: Chenhao deeply resented him; when Chenhao made demands Yifang refused, and Chenhao forced the garrison commander to impeach him and have him jailed in Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 明日，宸濠反，出以方，脅之降，不可，械舟中。

translations.literal: The next day Chen Hao rebelled, brought Yifang out, coerced him to surrender; he would not; he was shackled on a boat.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Chenhao rebelled, had Yifang brought out, and tried to force him to submit; when he refused, Chenhao had him shackled aboard a boat.

sentences.zh: 至安慶，兵敗，問地何名，舟子雲「黃石磯」，江西人音，則「王失機」也。

translations.literal: Reaching Anqing, his army was defeated; he asked what place this was called; the boatman said "Huangshi Ji" (Yellow Stone Jetty); in Jiangxi pronunciation this was "Wang shiji" (the king missed his opportunity).
translations.idiomatic: At Anqing, where his army was defeated, he asked the name of the place; the boatman answered "Yellow Stone Jetty"—which in the Jiangxi accent sounded like "the king has lost his chance."

sentences.zh: 宸濠以為不祥，斬以方祭江。

translations.literal: Chen Hao took it as inauspicious and beheaded Yifang to sacrifice to the river.
translations.idiomatic: Chenhao took this as an ill omen and beheaded Yifang as a sacrifice to the river.

sentences.zh: 後賊平，其子崇學求遺骸不得，斂衣冠歸葬。

translations.literal: After the rebels were pacified, his son Chongxue sought his remains but could not find them; he buried his clothing and cap in mourning and returned them for burial.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebellion was crushed, his son Chongxue could not recover his body and buried his clothing in lieu of the corpse.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖六年，巡撫陳洪謨上其事，詔贈光祿卿，蔭一子，立祠瑞州。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiajing Grand Coordinator Chen Hongmo reported the matter; an edict posthumously granted Yifang Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, yin privilege for one son, and a shrine erected in Ruizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Jiajing, Grand Coordinator Chen Hongmo memorialized the case; the throne posthumously made Yifang Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, granted hereditary privilege to one son, and ordered a shrine built in Ruizhou.

sentences.zh: 方宸濠之謀為變也，江西士民受害者不可勝紀。

translations.literal: When Chen Hao plotted rebellion, the scholars, officials, and common people of Jiangxi who suffered could not be fully counted.
translations.idiomatic: When Chenhao plotted rebellion, scholars, officials, and commoners across Jiangxi suffered beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 初遣閹校四出，籍民田廬，收縛豪強不附者。

translations.literal: At first he sent eunuch guards out in four directions to register the people's fields and houses and to seize and bind powerful men who would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: At first he sent eunuch agents out in every direction to register people's lands and dwellings and to seize local strongmen who refused to join him.

sentences.zh: 有萬木、鄭山，俱新建人，集鄉人結砦自固。

translations.literal: There were Wan Mu and Zheng Shan, both natives of Xinjian, who gathered their fellow villagers and built stockades to defend themselves.
translations.idiomatic: There were Wan Mu and Zheng Shan, both from Xinjian, who rallied their fellow villagers and built fortified stockades to hold their ground.

sentences.zh: 賊黨謝重一馳入村，二人執之，積葦張睢陽廟前，縛人馬，生焚之，濠黨不敢犯。

translations.literal: The rebel follower Xie Chongyi galloped into the village; the two men seized him, heaped reeds before the Suiyang Temple, bound him with his horse, and burned them alive—Chenhao's faction did not dare molest them.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebel follower Xie Chongyi galloped into the village, the two men seized him, heaped reeds before the Suiyang Temple, bound him together with his horse, and burned them alive. Chenhao's faction did not dare touch them.

sentences.zh: 二人飲江上，為盜淩十一所逼，趣見宸濠，烙而椎之，皆罵賊死。

translations.literal: The two men were drinking on the river when the bandit Ling Shiyi forced them to hurry before Chenhao; they were branded and clubbed, yet both cursed the bandits and died.
translations.idiomatic: The two men were drinking on the river when the bandit Ling Shiyi forced them to appear before Chenhao. They were branded and beaten with clubs, yet both cursed the rebels and died.

sentences.zh: 趙楠，南昌諸生。

translations.literal: Zhao Nan was a licentiate of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Nan was a licentiate of Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 兄模，嘗捐粟佐振。

translations.literal: His elder brother Mo had once donated grain to aid famine relief.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Mo had once donated grain to aid famine relief.

sentences.zh: 宸濠捕模索金，楠代往，脅之，不屈，被掠死。

translations.literal: Chenhao seized Mo and demanded gold; Nan went in his stead, was threatened, refused to submit, and was killed in the violence.
translations.idiomatic: Chenhao seized Mo and demanded gold. Nan went in his brother's place, was threatened, refused to yield, and was killed.

sentences.zh: 同邑辜增見迫，抗節不從，一家百口皆死。

translations.literal: Gu Zeng of the same county was pressed and held to his integrity without yielding; a household of a hundred mouths all perished.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Zeng of the same county was pressed to submit but held to his integrity and refused. His entire household of a hundred souls perished.

sentences.zh: 諸生劉世倫、儒士陳經官、義士李廣源，皆被掠，不屈死。

translations.literal: The licentiate Liu Shilun, the scholar Chen Jingguan, and the righteous man Li Guangyuan were all seized in the raids and died without yielding.
translations.idiomatic: The licentiate Liu Shilun, the scholar Chen Jingguan, and the righteous man Li Guangyuan were all seized in the raids and died without yielding.

sentences.zh: 葉景恩者，以俠聞，族居吳城。

translations.literal: Ye Jingen was famed for his chivalry; his clan dwelt at Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Jingen was famed for his chivalry, and his clan lived at Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 宸濠將作難，捕景恩，脅降之，不從，死獄中。

translations.literal: When Chenhao was about to raise rebellion he seized Jingen and threatened him to submit; Jingen refused and died in prison.
translations.idiomatic: When Chenhao was about to rebel, he seized Jingen and threatened him to submit. Jingen refused and died in prison.

sentences.zh: 宸濠兵過吳城，景恩弟景允以三百人邀擊賊。

translations.literal: When Chenhao's troops passed Wucheng, Jingen's younger brother Jingyun with three hundred men ambushed the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Chenhao's troops passed Wucheng, Jingen's younger brother Jingyun ambushed the rebels with three hundred men.

sentences.zh: 賊分兵焚劫景允家，其族景集、景修等四十九人皆死。

translations.literal: The rebels sent detachments to burn and plunder Jingyun's home; his clansmen Jingji, Jingxiu, and forty-nine others in all died.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sent detachments to burn and plunder Jingyun's home. His clansmen Jingji, Jingxiu, and forty-nine others in all perished.

sentences.zh: 又有閻順者，為寧府典寶副。

translations.literal: There was also Yan Shun, who served as deputy director of the Ning Princedom's Treasuries.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Yan Shun, deputy director of the Ning Princedom's Treasuries.

sentences.zh: 宸濠將反，順與典膳正陳宣、內使劉良微言不可，為典寶正塗欽所譖，三人懼誅，潛詣京師上變。

translations.literal: When Chenhao was about to rebel, Shun with the director of the princely kitchen Chen Xuan and the inner attendant Liu Liang privately said it must not be done; the director of treasuries Tu Qin slandered them, and the three, fearing execution, secretly went to the capital to report the plot.
translations.idiomatic: When Chenhao was about to rebel, Shun, together with the director of the princely kitchen Chen Xuan and the inner attendant Liu Liang, privately urged that it must not be done. The director of treasuries Tu Qin slandered them; fearing execution, the three secretly went to the capital to report the plot.

sentences.zh: 群小庇宸濠，下之獄，搒掠備至。

translations.literal: Petty men shielded Chenhao; the three were thrown into prison and tortured to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Petty men at court shielded Chenhao. The three were thrown into prison and tortured without mercy.

sentences.zh: 宸濠聞三人赴都，慮事泄，誣奏其罪，且嗾群小必殺之，會已遣戍孝陵，乃免。

translations.literal: When Chenhao heard the three had gone to the capital he feared exposure, falsely memorialized their crimes, and urged the petty men to kill them without fail; as it happened they had already been sent to garrison the Xiaoling Mausoleum, and so they escaped.
translations.idiomatic: When Chenhao learned the three had gone to the capital, he feared the plot would leak out. He falsely memorialized their crimes and urged the petty men at court to kill them without fail. As it happened, they had already been sent to garrison the Xiaoling Mausoleum, and so they were spared.

sentences.zh: 世宗立，復官。

translations.literal: When the Shizong emperor came to the throne, their offices were restored.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shizong emperor came to the throne, their offices were restored.
